$comment: Editorial descriptions of works, merged into each work's manifest at sync time by
scripts/sync-corpus.mjs and rendered by /documenta (and anywhere else reading
`manifest.description`).
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS RATHER THAN A FIELD IN the corpus's works/*/manifest.json: those
manifests are GENERATED. A re-parse rewrites them, so a description written there
survives exactly until the next parser fix — and this project fixes parsers by
re-parsing (CLAUDE.md's 're-parse, never re-crawl'). Descriptions are editorial, not
scraped, so they live in tracked source and are merged in on the way to the site. The
corpus stays purely generated and re-parsing stays free of consequences. Same posture,
same reasoning, and the same place as unpublished.json.
SHAPE: work id -> language -> { text, origin }. The outer key is the work being
described, so the two language editions of one document are described separately — a
description read from the Portuguese edition is prose about THAT text, not a translated
label. The inner key is the language the prose is written in, which is the work's own
language for a reading and any UI language for a translation of one.
ORIGIN IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THE SHAPE, and the two values are not interchangeable:
"read"       — written by READING THE DOCUMENT IN THE CORPUS. The rule in
docs/writing-descriptions.md is not negotiable: never from recollection
of what a document with that title probably says. A plausible-sounding
wrong description is worse than none, because nothing on the rendered
page distinguishes it from a real summary.
"translated" — derived from another rendering of the SAME work, named in `from`.
A translation is never written from the document; it inherits whatever
the reading got right and whatever it got wrong, which is exactly why
it is labelled rather than merged into the same field. `from` makes the
provenance a chain that can be checked: correct a reading and every
translation of it is known to be stale.
A work with no entry simply has no description; nothing renders a placeholder.

en.text: Pius XI's 1932 encyclical to the bishops of Mexico on the continuing persecution of the Church there, reviewing the government's anti-Catholic constitutional laws and broken pledges, addressing whether seeking state permission for worship compromises Catholic principle, urging the faithful toward Catholic Action, and praising clergy and laity who suffered for the faith.

Pius X's encyclical on the neglect of religious instruction, arguing that widespread ignorance of Christian doctrine — even among the educated — is the root of moral decline, and that teaching it is a pastor's first duty under the Council of Trent. It closes with six binding ordinances: weekly catechism for children, First Communion preparation, a parish Confraternity of Christian Doctrine, and adult instruction on holy days.

Pius XII's 1958 encyclical to the bishops, clergy and faithful of China, condemning the government-sponsored “Patriotic Association” that claims authority over episcopal appointments and doctrine. He reaffirms the Roman Pontiff's exclusive right to appoint bishops, declares that consecration without papal mandate incurs automatic excommunication, and expresses solidarity with Catholics enduring persecution.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Pio XII aos bispos e fiéis da China (1958), denunciando a «Associação patriótica» instituída pelo regime para afastar os católicos da Santa Sé sob pretexto de patriotismo, condenando a eleição e consagração de bispos sem mandato pontifício e exortando os perseguidos a permanecerem firmes na fé e em comunhão com Roma.

en.text: Benedict XV's first encyclical, issued three months into the First World War, appeals for an end to the fighting and traces its underlying causes to a decline in mutual charity, contempt for authority, and class conflict between rich and poor, naming love of money as their deepest root. It also calls on Catholics to abandon factional labels and remain united with their bishops, then closes with a prayer for peace.

Pius XII's encyclical on the reign of Mary, our Queen and Mother, over all created things. Draws on Scripture, patristic and liturgical witness, and the arguments of theology to establish that Mary's royal dignity flows from her divine motherhood and shared work with Christ, and, on that basis, institutes the feast of the Queenship of Mary, to be kept every 31 May.

pt.text: Encíclica de Pio XII sobre a realeza de Nossa Senhora: percorre os testemunhos da tradição patrística, da liturgia e da arte, e os argumentos teológicos — a maternidade divina, a cooperação na redenção — que fundamentam o título de rainha. Institui a festa de Maria Rainha, a celebrar-se em 31 de maio com a renovação da consagração da humanidade ao seu coração imaculado, como penhor de paz.

en.text: Pius XI's 1935 encyclical to the bishops on the Catholic priesthood, written for the fifty-sixth anniversary of his own ordination. It expounds the priest's dignity and sacramental powers — above all to forgive sins and confect the Eucharist — then treats the piety, chastity, poverty and learning proper formation must instill, and how a true vocation, usually rooted in a Christian family, is discerned and nurtured in the seminary.

Pius X marks the golden jubilee of the definition of the Immaculate Conception, urging renewed devotion to Mary as the surest way of restoring all things in Christ. He sets out her singular part in the work of redemption and her office as mediatrix of grace, calls the faithful to imitate her faith, hope and charity, and closes by proclaiming a jubilee indulgence with its conditions.

Addressed to the bishops of the East Indies, this 1893 letter recounts the settlement of the Portuguese patronato dispute that erected eight new dioceses under Goa's patriarchal see, and argues that a native clergy — not foreign missionaries alone — must be trained to secure the Church's future there. It closes appealing to European Catholics for funds to found and staff the needed seminaries.

John XXIII's first encyclical, written at the start of his pontificate around the recognition of truth, “a renewal of Christian morals,” and “a restoration of unity, harmony, and peace.” It addresses truth against error and the press's duties, unity among nations, within the family, and within the Church around the newly announced Ecumenical Council, then counsels bishops, clergy, religious, and the sick.

pt.text: Primeira carta encíclica de João XXIII, dirigida a todo o orbe católico, sobre o conhecimento da verdade, a restauração da unidade e da paz na caridade. Trata da verdade e do indiferentismo religioso, da concórdia entre povos, classes e famílias, da unidade da Igreja em torno da Cátedra de Pedro, e encerra com exortações paternais a bispos, clero, religiosos, missionários, pobres, refugiados e à Igreja perseguida.

it.text: Lettera enciclica di Pio XI per il XV centenario della morte di sant'Agostino d'Ippona. Ripercorre la sua conversione, la dottrina della grazia contro manichei, donatisti e pelagiani, l'immagine delle due città tratta da «Della città di Dio», e l'opera di fondatore di vita religiosa, esortando i fedeli a venerarne le reliquie a Pavia e a pregare in vista del Congresso Eucaristico di Cartagine.

en.text: Pius XII's 1954 encyclical to the bishops, clergy and faithful of China, written after the Apostolic Nuncio's expulsion and growing pressure on Chinese Catholics to make their Church independent of Rome in government, finances and doctrine. It insists that such independence is incompatible with the Church's divine constitution and its subjection to the Supreme Pontiff, defends the place of foreign missionaries, and urges perseverance under persecution.

Leo XIII's encyclical urging Catholics to devote the month of October to the Rosary, presenting it as the most effective prayer for the object then closest to his heart: the reconciliation of nations separated from the Church, above all in the Christian East. He recounts Mary's historic role as guardian of Church unity, from Dominic Guzman's preaching to earlier popes' efforts to spread the devotion in the East.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Leão XIII sobre o Rosário como via de retorno à unidade da Igreja. Pede orações perseverantes pela reconciliação dos povos separados do Oriente e do Ocidente, apresenta Maria — evocando o Concílio de Éfeso — como o vínculo capaz de reuni-los sob o Pontífice Romano, e anuncia a construção de um templo à Rainha do Rosário em Patras.

en.text: John XXIII's encyclical for the fifteenth centenary of the death of Pope St. Leo the Great, recounting Leo's life, his defense of the faith against the Nestorian and Pelagian heresies, and his teaching on the primacy of the Roman See as the center of the Church's visible unity. With the Second Vatican Council approaching, it turns that example into a renewed call for unity among all Christians.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de João XXIII pelo XV centenário da morte de são Leão Magno, papa e doutor da Igreja: sua vida, sua obra de pastor universal e luzeiro de doutrina, e a doutrina leonina sobre a unidade da Igreja em torno do bispo de Roma, sucessor de Pedro, evocada às vésperas do Concílio Vaticano II. Termina exortando ao retorno dos irmãos separados à unidade católica.

en.text: On the restoration of Christian philosophy, and specifically of St Thomas Aquinas, in Catholic schools. Leo XIII sets out philosophy's proper office as handmaid to faith, surveys what the Fathers and the Scholastics made of it, singles out Thomas as the master whose method keeps faith and reason each in its right, and directs bishops to make his doctrine the foundation of clerical and university teaching.

Leo XIII writes to the bishops of Canada on the Manitoba School Question, after the province's legislature abolished Catholic separate schools. He insists that education without religion cannot form good Christians or honest citizens, urges Catholic Canadians to set aside party divisions and act in union, and counsels accepting whatever partial redress is available while continuing to press for full justice.

Pius XII's Holy Year 1950 encyclical summoning a worldwide crusade of prayer against atheistic propaganda. It surveys an unsettled peace despite war's end, persecuted clergy, and a press that mocks religion and spreads vice, and calls on priests and Catholic Action to counter these evils, inviting the faithful to join him in prayer on Passion Sunday for a social order rebuilt on truth, justice, and charity.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Pio XII, escrita durante o Ano Santo de 1950, que convoca os fiéis a uma cruzada de orações pela renovação cristã dos costumes e pela concórdia entre os povos. Diante do ateísmo, das perseguições à Igreja e do risco de novos conflitos, o Papa pede orações públicas para o dia 26 de março, domingo da Paixão, unidas às suas na basílica de São Pedro.

en.text: Leo XIII announces the consecration of the entire human race to the Sacred Heart of Jesus, to be enacted the following June. He argues that Christ's kingship extends to all people, not only the baptized, both by natural right as the Son of God and by the right of redemption, and prescribes the prayers, litany and act of consecration to be observed.

Benedict XV renews, for a second Christmas, his appeal on behalf of the starving and disease-stricken children of Central Europe left destitute by the war. He asks that a collection be taken up on the feast of the Holy Innocents, or the preceding Sunday, for their relief, to be forwarded to him or to the Save the Children Fund, and pledges one hundred thousand lire of his own.

Leo XIII's encyclical to the bishops, clergy and people of Italy on Freemasonry's campaign against the Catholic religion there, tracing the sect's course from the overthrow of the Papal States to open irreligion, warning that abandoning the Christian faith exposes Italy to socialism and social ruin, and calling for renewed pastoral vigilance, popular resistance, and prayer to Mary and the Apostles Peter and Paul.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Leão XIII aos bispos, ao clero e ao povo da Itália sobre a ação da Maçonaria contra a Igreja Católica no país — a supressão das ordens religiosas, a confiscação dos bens eclesiásticos, a laicização da família e do ensino — e um apelo à fidelidade religiosa e à oração como caminho para o verdadeiro bem-estar da Itália.

en.text: Leo XIII's encyclical on Christian marriage: Christ raised it to a sacrament and restored the unity and indissolubility it had lost, so the Church holds authority over the marriages of the baptized. It argues against treating marriage as a merely civil contract subject to the state, sets out the evils that follow from divorce, and closes commending to the bishops those living outside a lawful bond.

Leo XIII's 1892 letter to the archbishops, bishops, clergy and faithful of France, urging Catholics to accept the Republic as the nation's constituted civil power while reserving the right to oppose unjust legislation. He rebuts the charge that Catholics seek political domination, upholds the Concordat, and condemns the proposed separation of Church and State as denying government's duty toward God.

Leo XIII's encyclical on the Confraternity of the Holy Rosary, written in his eighty-eighth year and framed as a dying father's repetition of Christ's “Behold, thy Mother.” It argues that the age's appetite for association is good in itself, that Catholics should meet it with sodalities rather than abandon it, and that the Rosary Society is the first of them — defending prayer to the saints as intercession rather than as a rival to prayer to God.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Leão XIII, de 1897, sobre o Rosário de Nossa Senhora, publicada por ocasião do mês de outubro. Recorda o lugar de Maria na Encarnação e na Redenção, recomenda a Confraria do Rosário e defende a eficácia da sua recitação em comum, a licitude da oração aos santos e a imitação dos anjos, e saúda a recente iniciativa do «Rosário perpétuo».

en.text: Leo XIII on the life and legacy of Francis of Assisi, marking the seventh centenary of his birth alongside St. Benedict's. It presents Francis as a living image of Christ, down to the stigmata, and commends the Third Order he founded — open to every age, rank, and sex — as the remedy for the era's strife between rich and poor, urging the faithful, and Italians especially, to enroll in it.

Pius XII invites the faithful, during the month traditionally dedicated to Mary, to public prayer for a peace still unsettled after the war and, particularly, for a just resolution of the dispute over Palestine and its Holy Places. He renews his wartime consecration of the human family to the Immaculate Heart of Mary and asks that the same consecration be repeated in every diocese and parish.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Pio XII pedindo que as orações do mês de maio, tradicionalmente dedicado a Nossa Senhora, sejam oferecidas em 1948 pela concórdia entre as nações após a guerra mundial e pela pacificação da Palestina, cujos lugares santos são então devastados por conflitos, renovando a consagração da família humana ao Coração Imaculado de Maria.

en.text: On integral human development in charity and truth, taking up Paul VI's Populorum Progressio forty years on. Charity in truth is set out as the principle of the Church's social doctrine and then applied: to the global financial crisis, to the ethics of business and the market, to gratuitousness and gift, to the environment, to cooperation between peoples, and to the human meaning of technology and bioethics.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Bento XVI que retoma a Populorum Progressio de Paulo VI, quarenta anos depois, para pensar o desenvolvimento integral dos povos à luz da caridade na verdade. Percorre a globalização, os direitos e deveres ligados ao ambiente, a colaboração entre nações e pessoas, e os riscos de um progresso técnico desligado de Deus e da verdade sobre o homem.

en.text: On the worldwide economic crisis and the spread of atheistic propaganda that exploits it, warning that irreligion and organized unbelief are turning social distress into rebellion against God. Calls the faithful to prayer, penance, and reparation to the Sacred Heart of Jesus as the remedy for the crisis and the disorder it has unleashed.

Leo XIII's 1898 encyclical to the bishops of Scotland, recalling the nation's Catholic heritage and inviting Scottish Protestants back to unity with Rome. It argues that Scripture cannot be safely interpreted by private judgment alone but requires the Church's living magisterium, defends the perpetuity of the Eucharistic sacrifice, and urges Scottish Catholics to support Catholic education, naming Blairs College.

Leo XIII's letter to the bishops of Poland, urging the Polish people to hold fast to the Catholic faith their ancestors defended. It calls for diligence in Christian marriage and education, rigorous seminary formation and study, and charity toward workers as in Rerum novarum, then addresses Poles under Russian rule, the house of Hapsburg, and the province of Gniezno-Poznan in turn.

Pius XI's encyclical on Christian marriage, organized around St. Augustine's three blessings of wedlock — offspring, conjugal faith, and the sacrament — expounding each in turn before cataloguing the errors attacking them: contraception, abortion, eugenic sterilization, divorce, and the “false emancipation” of women, and closing with remedies for restoring marriage to the divine plan.

Addressed to the Catholic missionaries in Africa, on the Church's long opposition to slavery and its wretched yoke. Leo XIII recalls papal predecessors who fought the institution, reports on his own efforts including a letter to the Brazilian bishops and Cardinal Lavigerie's mission against the African slave trade, and decrees an annual collection on the feast of the Epiphany to fund missions working to abolish slavery.

John Paul II re-reads Rerum Novarum on its centenary against the “new things” of 1989, the fall of Communism in Eastern Europe. He diagnoses socialism's core error, then treats the proper limits of private property and its universal destination, the free market's strengths and its moral limits, and the state's duty toward the common good, closing on the human person as the way the Church must walk.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de João Paulo II, no centenário da Rerum Novarum, que revê a doutrina social perante a queda dos regimes comunistas de 1989. Analisa o erro antropológico do socialismo, defende a propriedade privada e o destino universal dos bens, examina os limites do livre mercado perante necessidades sem poder de compra, e trata do Estado e da cultura, situando o homem como caminho da Igreja.

en.text: Paul VI asks the whole Church to pray the Rosary through October 1966 for peace, with war in eastern Asia and a nuclear arms race in view, invoking Mary as Queen of Peace. He presses the nations toward sincere negotiation, asks that 4 October — the anniversary of his appeal at the United Nations — be kept as a day of prayer, and closes with a Marian appeal for justice and a lasting peace.

pt.text: Convida os fiéis a rezarem o Rosário durante o mês de outubro para implorar o dom da paz, em meio à guerra e ao derramamento de sangue na Ásia oriental. Invoca a intercessão de Maria, Rainha da Paz e Mãe da Igreja, e institui o dia 4 de outubro, aniversário da viagem do Papa à ONU, como jornada de súplica pela paz.

en.text: Leo XIII's appeal to the world's bishops for renewed support of the Society for the Propagation of the Faith and the Society for the Schools of the East, arguing that reuniting the Eastern Churches with Rome — the goal of his recent letter Praeclara — requires trained clergy, schools, and Catholic literature suited to their own traditions, all of which mission funding must sustain.

An appeal for the month of May 1945, three weeks before the war in Europe ended: Pius XII asks the faithful, and children in particular, to pray to Mary for peace and for the renewal of Christian morals on which peace rests, and to pray for refugees, prisoners and the wounded — so that what follows the devastation may be a just peace and not one carrying the seed of future wars.

pt.text: Encíclica de Pio XII, publicada em plena Segunda Guerra Mundial, convocando os fiéis — sobretudo as crianças — a rezar durante o mês de maio, dedicado à Virgem, pelo fim do conflito e por uma paz fundada na justiça e na caridade, e não apenas na vingança. Lembra também os refugiados, os prisioneiros nos campos de concentração e os doentes da guerra.

en.text: Pius X marks the eighth centenary of the death of St. Anselm of Canterbury, praising his sanctity and his stand for the Church's liberty against secular encroachment, then holds him up as founder of a scholastic middle way between rationalist excess and fideist neglect — deployed as a direct warning against modernist "agnosticism" and dialecticians who overreach reason's limits.

Leo XIII writes to the bishops of Hungary amid recent state laws he judges hostile to the Church's rights and the Catholic faith. He urges fidelity to papal teaching, warns against the dangers of mixed marriages, and calls for annual meetings of Catholic laymen, a vigilant Catholic press, strong Catholic schools, and the revival of clergy and lay confraternities to safeguard religion.

Leo XIII to the bishops of Spain, where rival Catholic political factions had fractured the unity the country once showed the Church. He calls for full obedience to bishops, draws a line between religion and politics without divorcing the two, directs the clergy to stay clear of party strife, and places Catholic associations and the Catholic press under their bishops' direction as the way back to that lost concord.

Leo XIII's encyclical addressed to the Italian people, following up his 1884 Humanum genus, on Freemasonry's inroads into Italy since unification: its substitution of naturalism for the faith, its capture of schools and civic life, and its corruption of workers' and mutual-aid societies. He orders Catholics to leave masonic and affiliated societies, resist through their own press, schools and associations, and pray for the Church's deliverance.

Pius XII's brief encyclical of 5 November 1956 lamenting the renewed Soviet crackdown in Hungary, days after his prior appeal for peace. He condemns the bloodshed and the violent overthrow of newly restored institutions, invokes Cain's cry of his brother's blood from Genesis 4:10 over the Hungarian dead, and calls all peoples to a justice-based peace while praying for those slain.

Pius XII's letter to the bishops of the world, prompted by decades of petitions asking that the Blessed Virgin Mary's bodily Assumption into heaven be defined as a dogma of faith. Rather than defining it himself, the pope asks each bishop to report on the devotion of his clergy and people to the Assumption, and whether he judges the doctrine fit for solemn definition.

pt.text: Carta de Pio XII aos bispos, pedindo-lhes parecer sobre a oportunidade de definir como dogma de fé a assunção corporal da Bem-Aventurada Virgem Maria aos céus. Invoca as numerosas súplicas recebidas pela Sé Apostólica desde 1849 e o voto de quase duzentos padres do Concílio Vaticano, e pergunta a cada bispo que devoção o seu clero e povo tributam a esse mistério e se desejam vê-lo definido.

en.text: Leo XIII's encyclical to the bishops and clergy of France on forming priests. It sets a curriculum: classical letters for junior seminaries, then rational philosophy grounded in Aeterni Patris against modern errors, scholastic theology built on St. Thomas's Summa, the Roman Catechism, Scripture, Church history and canon law for senior ones — then turns to ordained priests, urging obedience to their bishops and zeal tempered by prudence.

On the meaning of Christian love: it follows eros and agape from their ancient distinction to their unity in biblical revelation and the Incarnation, then turns to the Church's charitable activity — alongside proclaiming the word and celebrating the sacraments — as belonging to her own nature, its relation to justice and its organisation, closing with the saints and Mary as the exemplars of charity.

pt.text: Trata do amor cristão a partir de « Deus é amor » (1 Jo 4, 16): a primeira parte busca a unidade entre eros e agape na criação e na história da salvação, culminando no amor a Deus e ao próximo revelados em Jesus Cristo; a segunda volta-se para a caritas como prática da Igreja enquanto « comunidade de amor », discutindo justiça, caridade e seus responsáveis.

en.text: Pius XI's 1933 letter to the Spanish hierarchy denouncing the new Republic's laws on religious confessions and congregations — the dissolution of the Society of Jesus, the seizure of church property, and the laicizing of education — and urging clergy and faithful to prayer and to unity in Catholic Action.

Francis's 2024 encyclical on devotion to the Sacred Heart of Jesus: what the symbol of the 'heart' can still mean for a distracted age, what Christ's own gaze, words and pierced side reveal about his human and divine love, the history of this devotion from Margaret Mary through Francis de Sales, Claude de la Colombière, Charles de Foucauld and Thérèse of Lisieux, and how reparation for love unreturned extends into fraternity, mission and social concern.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Francisco sobre o amor humano e divino do Coração de Jesus. Parte do sentido bíblico e espiritual do coração, passa pela devoção ao Coração de Cristo em místicos como Santa Margarida Maria, São Francisco de Sales e Santa Teresa do Menino Jesus, e termina pedindo que esse amor se prolongue no amor fraterno e na reparação, ligando o documento a Laudato si' e Fratelli tutti.

en.text: Leo XIII's encyclical on the Rosary, reviewing the annual Rosary letters he has issued since 1883 and the honors he has attached to the devotion — its October dedication, its place in the Roman Breviary, the invocation added to the Litany of Loreto — and surveying the indulgences it carries. It announces his intention to issue a “Constitution” setting out the rights and privileges of the Rosary Sodality.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Leão XIII que resume os documentos pontifícios sobre o Rosário mariano publicados desde 1883, recordando a sua origem celeste, a instituição da festa e do mês de Outubro a ele consagrado, e o tesouro de indulgências concedido às Confrarias do Rosário; anuncia uma Constituição sobre os direitos e privilégios dessas Confrarias.

en.text: On the origin of civil power, written after a run of attacks on the lives of European rulers. Leo XIII rejects the doctrine that authority is merely delegated by popular will, traces the ruler's power to God through Scripture and the Fathers, bounds obedience by the higher duty to divine and natural law, recalls the Church's deference toward pagan and Christian rulers alike, and asks bishops to preach this against sedition.

On the mercy of God, revealed above all in Christ crucified and risen and read through the parable of the prodigal son. It follows mercy from the covenant with Israel to the Paschal Mystery, weighs it against the anxieties of the modern world and against the demand for justice alone, and closes asking the Church to proclaim mercy, to practise it, and to beg for it from generation to generation.

pt.text: Encíclica de João Paulo II sobre a misericórdia de Deus revelada por Cristo — «quem me vê, vê o Pai». Percorre a misericórdia no Antigo Testamento, a parábola do filho pródigo como sua imagem central, e o mistério pascal como sua plenitude. Considera as ameaças do mundo contemporâneo e conclui apelando à Igreja para invocar, pela oração, a misericórdia divina diante do mal que ameaça a humanidade.

en.text: Pius XI's encyclical on the Christian education of youth. It sets out who holds the right and duty to educate — the Church by a supernatural title, the family by nature, and the State subordinately, for the common good — condemns pedagogical naturalism and mixed sex-education, and treats the family, the Church and a genuinely Christian school as the proper environment for education, with Christ as its teacher and model.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Pio XI sobre a educação cristã da juventude: a quem compete a missão de educar — Igreja, família e Estado, em harmonia —, o sujeito da educação, o homem decaído mas remido, contra o naturalismo pedagógico, a educação sexual e a co-educação, o ambiente que a envolve, e o fim e a forma da educação cristã, tendo Jesus Cristo por Mestre e Modelo.

en.text: Pius XI's encyclical on atheistic communism, written as its persecution intensified in Russia, Mexico and Spain. It traces communism's Marxist materialism, how it strips man of liberty and dignity and would dissolve family and property into a collectivity built for production, opposes to it the Church's teaching on God, man and society, and prescribes remedies — renewed Christian life, social justice, Catholic Action — under St. Joseph's protection.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Pio XI sobre o comunismo ateu, escrita quando a sua perseguição já lavrava na Rússia, no México e na Espanha. Expõe a doutrina comunista e o seu materialismo marxista, com frutos deploráveis como a luta contra tudo o que se chama Deus e o terrorismo, opondo-lhe a doutrina católica sobre Deus, o homem e a sociedade, e indicando remédios: renovação da vida cristã, justiça social e Ação Católica.

en.text: On biblical studies, fifty years after Leo XIII's Providentissimus Deus. Pius XII directs Catholic exegetes to work from the original Hebrew, Greek and Aramaic rather than from the Vulgate alone, to use textual criticism, and to identify the literary genres of the ancient Near East before judging what a passage means — closing with an appeal that priests draw their preaching and their own spiritual life from Scripture.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Pio XII, publicada no cinquentenário da Providentissimus Deus de Leão XIII, sobre os estudos bíblicos. Recorda o incentivo dado por Leão XIII, Pio X e Pio XI à ciência bíblica e fixa critérios hermenêuticos para a exegese católica: uso dos textos originais e da crítica textual, busca do sentido literal antes do espiritual, atenção aos géneros literários e uso da Escritura no ensino dos fiéis.

en.text: Leo XIII's encyclical on the Holy Spirit: it sets out the Catholic doctrine of the Blessed Trinity, then traces the Holy Ghost's action in Christ's Incarnation, in the founding and animation of the Church, and in the sanctification of individual souls through grace and the sacraments. It closes by urging devotion to the Holy Ghost and decreeing an annual novena of prayer to Him before Pentecost in every parish church.

Pius XII's encyclical marking the eighth centenary of the death of St. Bernard of Clairvaux, 'the last of the Fathers.' It surveys his teaching drawn from Scripture and the Fathers, his eloquent style, his union of contemplative prayer with vigorous action defending papal authority and combating heresy, and his devotion to Christ and the Virgin Mary, commending him as a model of charity for the Church.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Pio XII pelo VIII centenário da morte de São Bernardo de Claraval, louvando o "doutor melífluo": sua doutrina extraída da Escritura e dos Padres, seu estilo suave e ardente, sua vida contemplativa unida à ação enérgica na defesa da autoridade pontifícia e da fé, seu amor a Cristo e devoção filial à Mãe de Deus — convidando todos a imitar suas virtudes.

en.text: On the Holy Spirit, completing the Trinitarian sequence begun with Redemptor Hominis on the Son and Dives in Misericordia on the Father. In three parts it follows the Spirit given at the Supper and at Pentecost, his work of convincing the world concerning sin — including the sin against the Holy Spirit — and his office as the giver of life, with the Jubilee of the third millennium in view.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de João Paulo II sobre o Espírito Santo, que dá continuidade às precedentes Redemptor Hominis e Dives in Misericordia. Em três partes, trata do Espírito dado pelo Pai e pelo Filho à Igreja, do Espírito que convence o mundo do pecado — incluindo o pecado contra o próprio Espírito Santo — e do Espírito que dá a vida, à luz do Jubileu do ano 2000.

en.text: Leo XIII's brief encyclical to the Archbishop of Quito and the bishops of Ecuador, condemning that country's new civil marriage and divorce laws. It restates the Church's teaching that Christian marriage, raised by Christ to a sacrament, is indissoluble and falls under ecclesiastical rather than civil authority, and urges the bishops to persevere in defending the Church's rights despite the legislation already enacted.

Pius X's inaugural encyclical, taking the Apostle's phrase "to restore all things in Christ" as the whole programme of his pontificate. He reads his age's apostasy from God as a deep-rooted disease, makes the Church the way back to Christ, and asks bishops for holy priests, well-governed seminaries, patient religious instruction, and charity rather than bitterness toward those estranged.

John Paul II's encyclical on the Eucharist as the mystery from which the Church draws her life. It traces the sacrament's institution at the Last Supper as the sacrifice of the Cross perpetuated, argues that the Eucharist both builds the Church and expresses her apostolicity and communion, addresses the dignity owed to its celebration, and closes by presenting Mary as “Woman of the Eucharist”.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de João Paulo II sobre a Eucaristia na sua relação com a Igreja. Apresenta o sacrifício eucarístico como mistério de fé e memorial da paixão do Senhor, mostra como a Eucaristia edifica e manifesta a apostolicidade da Igreja através do sacerdócio ministerial, trata da comunhão eclesial e das condições para a concelebração, exorta ao decoro na celebração litúrgica e propõe Maria, «mulher eucarística», como modelo de fé eucarística.

en.text: Pius XII's 1954 encyclical for the twelfth centenary of the martyrdom of St. Boniface, apostle of Germany. It recounts his mission from England under Rome's mandate, his preaching in Friesland, Thuringia, Franconia and Bavaria, the founding of Fulda as a house of prayer and learning, his reform of the Frankish church as papal legate, and his death at pagan hands — holding up his obedience to the Holy See as the model.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Pio XII aos bispos da Inglaterra, Alemanha, Áustria, Bélgica e Holanda, pelo décimo-segundo centenário do martírio de são Bonifácio. Narra a vida do apóstolo da Frísia e da Germânia — sua obediência à Sé Apostólica, o mosteiro de Fulda, o martírio entre os frísios — e propõe aos fiéis sua fidelidade romana e confiança na graça divina como exemplo.

it.text: Nel terzo centenario del martirio di san Giosafat, arcivescovo di Polock, l'enciclica ripercorre lo scisma bizantino degli Slavi orientali e l'unione di Brest del 1596, poi la vita di Giosafat, monaco basiliano e vescovo, ucciso nel 1623 per la causa dell'unità. Pio XI lo propone come patrono dei cattolici e dei dissidenti orientali, invitandoli alla preghiera e alla reciproca conoscenza in vista del ritorno alla piena comunione con la Sede Apostolica.

en.text: Paul VI's first encyclical, written one year into his pontificate as a statement of governing priorities: the Church's need for deeper self-awareness, the renewal called for by the Second Vatican Council, and dialogue with the world. The final and longest part elaborates dialogue as method, extending it outward through concentric circles — from all mankind, to believers in one God, to other Christians, to Catholics themselves.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Paulo VI sobre os caminhos que a Igreja deve seguir no mundo contemporâneo. Divide-se em três partes: a consciência que a Igreja deve aprofundar de si mesma e da sua missão, a renovação da sua vida interior, e o diálogo da salvação com a humanidade, distinguindo três círculos concêntricos — tudo o que é humano, os crentes em Deus e os cristãos separados.

en.text: Marking the third centenary of St. Charles Borromeo's canonization, Pius X holds him up as the model of true reform: fidelity to Rome and self-effacing zeal against heresy, opposed both to the Protestant revolt Borromeo fought and to what Pius calls the apostasy of his own day. It contrasts the true reformer, who trusts God and the Church, with the false one, who seeks his own glory, closing with an appeal to Catholic Action.

Leo XIII's short letter to the bishops of Ireland, praising the Irish Catholics' steadfast endurance under hardship, defending his recent counsel and decree to them as meant in truth and justice rather than interference, and announcing gifts of vestments and sacred vessels sent to Ireland's cathedral churches.

Leo XIII's encyclical to the bishops of Italy, confronting a “pernicious sect” exploiting the country's altered political condition to strip away its Christian institutions. Recalling Italy's historic debts to the papacy, it charges the bishops to rouse Catholic courage through associations, a sound press against hostile journalism, and rigorously formed seminaries, closing with an appeal to Mary and the saints.

Pius XII's encyclical marking the twenty-fifth anniversary of Pius XI's Rerum Ecclesiae, surveying the growth of Catholic missions worldwide and calling for the formation of a native clergy, respect for local cultures and traditions, and continued charitable and educational works. It urges clergy, religious and laity — especially Catholic Action — to sustain missionary vocations through prayer, formation and material support.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Pio XII sobre o fomento das missões, no 25º aniversário da Rerum Ecclesiae de Pio XI. Revê os progressos e perseguições da causa missionária e traça normas para o missionário: erguer entre os povos evangelizados uma Igreja com hierarquia e clero nativos, apoiada por Ação Católica, escolas, imprensa e assistência sanitária e social.

en.text: John Paul II on the value and inviolability of human life, setting the “Gospel of life” against what he calls a “culture of death”. Reading Genesis 4 as an image of violence against life, he surveys the threats from abortion to euthanasia, affirms “you shall not kill” as sacred and inviolable law, and calls for a new culture of life, closing with an appeal to Mary.

pt.text: Sobre o valor da vida humana e a sua inviolabilidade, diante das novas ameaças do aborto e da eutanásia: parte do grito do sangue de Abel e do eclipse do sentido da vida, percorre o mandamento «não matarás» perante a lei civil e a lei moral, e chama a uma nova cultura da vida, terminando com uma prece a Maria, Mãe dos viventes.

en.text: Leo XIII's encyclical marking the close of the year in which he celebrated his golden priestly jubilee. Taking the widespread demonstrations of devotion as an occasion, he diagnoses an age corrupted by rationalism, materialism and the socialism and atheism they breed, and calls the faithful — the clergy above all, by example — back to self-denial, prayer and the imitation of Christ.

Benedict XV's encyclical for the seventh centenary of the death of St. Dominic, commending the Order of Preachers to the whole Church. It traces three marks of Dominican preaching — solid doctrine, fidelity to the Apostolic See, and devotion to the Virgin through the Rosary — recalling Dominic's disputations against heresy at Toulouse, the four popes drawn from his order, and St. Pius V's victory at Lepanto.

Pius XII's 1957 encyclical on the missions, especially in Africa, describing the continent's rapid political and social change, the shortage of priests and material means in newly founded mission stations, and appealing to bishops of the older Christian nations to send diocesan priests, prayer, and financial support, plus lay Catholic Action workers, to the African missions.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Pio XII sobre a situação das missões católicas, sobretudo na África: descreve as alegrias e dificuldades do apostolado missionário no continente, convoca toda a Igreja à cooperação e detalha o tríplice dever dos fiéis para com as missões — oração, caridade e fomento das vocações missionárias — antes de estender o apelo às missões de todo o mundo.

en.text: Leo XIII's encyclical on the Rosary, urging its recitation as a proven form of communal prayer. He explains Mary's role as mediatrix under Christ the one Mediator, the Rosary's power to nourish faith when it is daily exposed to attack, and its indulgences for the living and the dead, closing with an appeal to pray the Rosary throughout October for the reunion of separated Christians with the Church.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Leão XIII sobre o Rosário de Nossa Senhora, dada em Roma a 20 de setembro de 1896. Recomenda essa oração pela eficácia da perseverança e da união de muitos numa só súplica, expõe Maria como mediadora e mestra de fé e penitência, e apela à sua recitação, sobretudo em outubro, para alcançar a reunião dos cristãos dissidentes com a Igreja.

en.text: John Paul II's 1998 encyclical on the relationship between faith and reason, opened by the image of ‘two wings’ lifting the human spirit toward truth. It traces their kinship in Scripture's wisdom literature, the Church's engagement with Greek philosophy, Aquinas's harmony of the two and their modern separation, then turns to the Magisterium's care for philosophy and to theology's present tasks, a century after Aeterni Patris.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de João Paulo II sobre a relação entre fé e razão — as duas asas pelas quais o espírito humano se eleva à contemplação da verdade, na imagem que abre o texto. Percorre o diálogo entre teologia e filosofia desde os Apóstolos até à reflexão contemporânea, sem canonizar nenhuma corrente filosófica, e termina apelando a teólogos e filósofos para recuperarem a dimensão metafísica da verdade.

en.text: Leo XIII's letter to the bishops of Italy on the formation of the clergy, urging seminaries to safeguard traditional doctrinal and spiritual formation against novelty and socialist influence, to maintain firm discipline and piety among seminarians, and to prepare priests versed in Christian social teaching who serve the people without engaging directly in political agitation.

Pius XI's 1937 letter to the bishops of Mexico amid the persecution of the Church there, praising the clergy's and faithful's constancy under trial and urging two remedies: the holiness of priests and the disciplined formation of the laity through Catholic Action. It sets principles for the legitimate defense of religious liberty and closes commending Mexico to Our Lady of Guadalupe.

On fraternity and social friendship, opening from St Francis of Assisi's love that crossed every border. It surveys a closed and throwaway world of nationalism and fear, reads the Good Samaritan as the call to an open society built on solidarity and the rights of peoples, and argues for a political charity against populism, for dialogue and forgiveness after conflict, against war and the death penalty, and for fraternity between religions.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Francisco sobre a fraternidade e a amizade social, inspirada no apelo de São Francisco de Assis, de quem toma o título. Parte da parábola do bom samaritano para denunciar as sombras dum mundo fechado e propor a política melhor, o diálogo e a amizade social, e o papel das religiões ao serviço da fraternidade no mundo.

en.text: Pius XII's encyclical proclaiming a Marian Year to mark the centenary of Pius IX's 1854 definition of the Immaculate Conception. It recounts the dogma's proclamation, the Lourdes apparitions that seemed to confirm it, and its bond with the newly defined dogma of the Assumption, and calls the Church to a year of prayer for its own freedom and for peace among nations.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Pio XII que, no centenário da definição dogmática da Imaculada Conceição, expõe os fundamentos bíblicos e patrísticos dessa doutrina e proclama um Ano Mariano. Convoca os fiéis a peregrinações, orações e penitência por intenções como a juventude, a paz entre os povos e a união dos cristãos separados, sob a proteção da Virgem Maria.

en.text: Pius XII's encyclical for the fourteenth centenary of the death of St. Benedict of Nursia, recounting his youth in Rome, his years as a hermit at Subiaco, and his founding of Monte Cassino, then expounding the Rule and its balance of prayer, labor, and hospitality. It credits the Benedictines with preserving learning as the Roman Empire collapsed, and closes appealing for the rebuilding of Monte Cassino, destroyed in the recent war.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Pio XII pelo XIV centenário da morte de São Bento, patriarca dos monges do Ocidente: traça a figura histórica do santo, os benefícios de sua Regra e de sua Ordem para a Igreja e a civilização, e os ensinamentos da Regra beneditina para o mundo contemporâneo, encerrando com um apelo à restauração do mosteiro de Montecassino, destruído pela guerra.

en.text: An account of Sts Cyril and Methodius, the ninth-century brothers sent from Constantinople to the Slavs of Moravia: their formation, their commission from Rome, the charge that a liturgy in the Slavonic tongue broke with Church custom — answered and allowed in Rome — and their deaths. Leo XIII extends their feast to the universal Church on 5 July and asks their intercession for reconciliation with the East.

John XXIII on the October Rosary, recalling that Leo XIII and Pius XII had made the same appeal before him. He asks prayers for the missionaries about to leave for the foreign missions and for the centenary of the North American College, for rulers weighing the causes of international discord, against the errors of laicism and materialism, and for the coming Roman Synod and Ecumenical Council.

pt.text: Primeira encíclica de João XXIII (26 de setembro de 1959), exortando os fiéis à reza do Rosário durante outubro, na linha do apelo de Leão XIII e de Pio XII à mesma devoção mariana. Pede orações pelas missões — recordando o envio de jovens missionários e o centenário do Colégio Americano do Norte — e pela paz, associando a intenção do próximo Sínodo de Roma e do Concílio Ecumênico.

en.text: Leo XIII settles the name "Christian Democracy" for Catholic charitable action among the working classes, distinguishing it sharply from Social Democracy: it rests on faith, upholds private property and the distinctions of rank, and carries no political meaning or preference for one form of government over another. He urges bishops and Catholics to unite in this work, avoid partisan disputes, and combine material relief with religious and moral formation of the poor.

A letter to the Patriarch of Lisbon and the bishops of Portugal, commending their joint protest against the Portuguese government's decrees against religious orders. Leo XIII defends the right of religious institutes to exist and of the faithful to embrace that state of life, insists any conformity to civil law leave vows and novitiate intact, and calls on the bishops to unite Catholic forces in defending the Church's rights.

Pius X's follow-up to Vehementer Nos, addressed to the French bishops after the 1905 separation law. It rules that the associations of worship the law requires cannot be formed without violating the Church's divine constitution and the rights of pope and bishops over ecclesiastical property, and directs the bishops instead to organize worship through whatever lawful means remain open to them.

Pius XII's encyclical on devotion to the Sacred Heart of Jesus, issued for the centenary of the feast's institution. It grounds the devotion in Scripture and the Fathers, argues that the Heart symbolizes Christ's threefold love — divine, spiritual and human — shown in the Eucharist, in Mary and in the Church, and exhorts the faithful to renewed practice through love, reparation and consecration.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Pio XII sobre o culto ao Sagrado Coração de Jesus, escrita para o centenário da instituição da festa por Pio IX. Percorre os fundamentos desse culto nas Escrituras do Antigo e do Novo Testamento, na tradição dos Padres e no seu desenvolvimento histórico até à Idade Média, e conclui exortando os fiéis a praticá-lo com maior fervor.

en.text: Paul VI on the regulation of birth, in three parts: the Church's competence to interpret the natural moral law, the doctrinal principles, and pastoral directives. It rests on an inseparable connection between the unitive and procreative meanings of the marriage act, excluding abortion, sterilisation and contraception while permitting recourse to infertile periods, and asks scientists for a more secure knowledge of natural rhythms.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Paulo VI sobre a regulação da natalidade. Reafirma a ligação inseparável entre união e procriação no ato conjugal, defende a paternidade responsável e exclui como ilícitos o aborto, a esterilização direta e os métodos artificiais de contracepção, admitindo apenas o recurso aos períodos infecundos. Termina com apelos aos governantes, cientistas, esposos, médicos, sacerdotes e bispos.

en.text: Benedict XV on preaching: never have there been more preachers, he observes, and never has the harvest been thinner. He blames men who run unsent, preach themselves and hunt applause, asks bishops to weigh character and learning before granting faculties as strictly as for confessors, and holds up St Paul — conformed to God's will, a man of prayer, preaching Christ crucified — as the measure.

Pius XII's encyclical against the “new theology” and related errors he judges corrosive of Catholic doctrine, including dogmatic relativism and philosophical novelty threatening scholastic theology. It permits scholarly inquiry into the bodily evolution of man from pre-existing matter, while ruling polygenism incompatible with original sin, and defends the historical substance of Genesis's opening chapters against overly free reinterpretation.

pt.text: Encíclica de Pio XII contra opiniões falsas que ameaçam a doutrina católica: evolucionismo panteísta, historicismo relativista e o desprezo pela teologia, pelo magistério, pela Escritura e pela filosofia escolástica entre alguns católicos. Admite discutir a origem do corpo humano a partir de matéria preexistente, mas rejeita o poligenismo, incompatível com o pecado original transmitido por geração a partir de um único Adão.

en.text: Leo XIII's encyclical on Freemasonry, framing history as a struggle between two opposed kingdoms and naming Freemasonry as the organizing centre of a wider network of secret societies. It traces their doctrine to naturalism and the denial of revelation, which it holds corrodes marriage, education and civil authority, and prescribes religious instruction, the revival of workers' guilds, and the Third Order of St. Francis.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Leão XIII sobre a Maçonaria, que apresenta a história como luta entre duas cidades opostas — a terrena e a celestial — e identifica a seita dos maçons como centro de uma rede de sociedades secretas. Atribui a sua doutrina ao naturalismo, que corrompe o casamento, a educação e a autoridade civil, e propõe remédios: instrução religiosa, associações de trabalhadores e a Ordem Terceira de São Francisco.

en.text: Pius X to the Portuguese hierarchy, condemning the Republic's Law of Separation of Church and State, which strips the Church of its property, subjects worship to lay associations under state control, forbids bishops to publish or act without government leave, and severs their ties to Rome. He declares the law null and void, praises the clergy's resistance, and urges bishops everywhere to support them.

Leo XIII's encyclical to the archbishops and bishops of Prussia on relations between the Holy See and Germany after years of hostile legislation. It praises German Catholics' fidelity under those laws, restates the Church's right to govern its seminaries and inner life, addresses relations with civil authority, and encourages missionary work in Germany's colonies before closing with an exhortation to unity and loyalty to Rome.

Written to the Italian bishops to organise the lay Catholic works — what came to be called Catholic Action — under the single aim of restoring all things in Christ. Pius X defines the movement's scope, ties its social work to Rerum Novarum, prescribes a Popular Union to hold it together, repeats the ban on direct participation in politics, and subordinates every such work to the bishops.

Leo XIII's encyclical on the Christian constitution of states: civil authority comes from God, not from the sovereignty of the people, and is bound to honor religion publicly. Rejecting the naturalist doctrines that exclude God from public life, it sets out the concord due between Church and State, and closes urging Catholics to take an active part in public affairs despite lawful disagreement over forms of government.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Leão XIII sobre a constituição cristã dos Estados: defende que o poder público só pode vir de Deus, expõe a Igreja como sociedade perfeita e soberana na sua esfera própria, distinta mas harmónica com o poder civil, refuta a tese liberal de separar os negócios da Igreja dos do Estado, e conclui exortando os católicos à unidade na participação da vida política.

en.text: A jubilee letter to Cardinal Gibbons and the bishops of the United States marking the twenty-fifth year of Leo XIII's pontificate. He thanks them for their tribute, praises the flourishing growth of Catholicism under religious liberty in America, commends their work founding schools and seminaries and their missionary outreach to Black and Native American communities, and their generosity toward the needs of the Holy See.

For the twelfth centenary of St Boniface's mission to Germany, written to the German hierarchy amid the disorder that followed the First World War. Benedict XV retraces Boniface's oath of fidelity to the Holy See, his correspondence with successive popes and his martyrdom, holds them up as the pattern of Germany's ancient union with Rome, urges its restoration, and grants indulgences for the centenary.

Leo XIII's encyclical to the bishops of Austria, urging them to hold annual episcopal conferences to coordinate their defense of the Church against anti-Catholic agitation, unite the faithful behind the hierarchy and the Roman Pontiff, strengthen seminary formation, encourage a Catholic press, and attend to the plight of workers as part of the social question.

Pius XII's appeal, amid the 1948 war in Palestine, for prayer for peace and for the safety of the Holy Places. He recounts his efforts at impartial mediation and aid to refugees, recalls the call to prayer he made in his recent encyclical Auspicia Quaedam, and proposes giving Jerusalem an international status guaranteeing free access to its sanctuaries and freedom of worship there.

pt.text: Pio XII renova, pela segunda vez, o apelo a orações públicas pela paz na Palestina, lamentando a destruição de lugares sagrados e o sofrimento de refugiados na guerra em curso. Defende um estatuto internacional para Jerusalém e arredores, e garantias internacionais de livre acesso aos lugares santos e de liberdade de culto, concedendo a bênção apostólica.

en.text: Leo XIII's letter to the bishops of Brazil, prompted by Brazil's abolition of slavery, arguing that slavery contradicts the natural and divine order and surveying the Church's campaign against it — patristic teaching on Christian equality, papal condemnations of the trade under Pius II, Paul III and Gregory XVI — before denouncing the overland slave trade still running in Africa and counselling the newly freed and their former masters.

Benedict XV's encyclical for the sixth centenary of Dante Alighieri's death, addressed to Catholic professors and students of literature. It presents Dante as a lifelong exemplar of Catholic faith whose Divine Comedy embodies Scripture, Christian philosophy and theology, and sound principles of civil government, and urges renewed devotion to his study against systems of education that exclude God.

Pius XI's 1937 encyclical urging renewed recitation of the Holy Rosary, especially through October, as recourse against the era's gravest dangers — class conflict, totalitarian statism, and above all Communism. He recommends daily family recitation before an image of Mary, gives thanks for his own recovered health through the intercession of St. Thérèse of Lisieux, and protests a public insult to the Virgin.

Pius XII's appeal for the annual month of the Rosary, written amid the post-war persecution of the Church and threats to the innocence of children. He urges the faithful to renew their trust in Mary through the Rosary, commends its daily recitation within the family as the safeguard of the Christian home, and asks prayers for bishops and others imprisoned or exiled for the faith.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Pio XII, publicada às vésperas do mês de outubro de 1951, que exorta os fiéis à recitação do terço mariano diante dos males do tempo — perseguições contra a Igreja e ameaças à inocência das crianças. Insiste no valor do terço rezado em família como escola de virtude cristã e força da Igreja, e pede orações pelos bispos e famílias perseguidos e encarcerados.

en.text: Leo XIII's letter to the bishops of Italy warning that Freemasonry endangers the Catholic faith there, urging the recovery of Italians drawn into the sect through ambition, faint-heartedness, or ignorance, and calling the clergy and faithful to renewed vigilance and resolute action against its designs.

Pius XI's encyclical on the persecution of the Catholic Church in Mexico under the 1917 Constitution and its 1926 enforcement laws, which stripped the Church of civil status, barred clergy from teaching, expelled foreign priests and religious, and closed schools and seminaries. He reviews the resistance of Mexico's bishops, clergy, and lay organizations, and commends the country to Our Lady of Guadalupe.

Leo XIII's first encyclical, written days into his pontificate: a survey of the evils he sees oppressing society — the subversion of first truths, contempt for lawful authority, family life corrupted — traced to the setting aside of the Church's authority, and answered by recalling what the papacy has done for civilization and by pressing bishops toward a Christian education of youth begun at home.

pt.text: Primeira encíclica de Leão XIII, sobre os males que assolam a sociedade moderna — a rejeição da autoridade da Igreja e do Pontífice Romano —, sua causa e seus remédios: a caridade fraterna, o respeito à autoridade eclesiástica, a restauração do Poder Temporal dos Papas, a fidelidade à Santa Sé Apostólica, a reforma do lar cristão e a reforma dos costumes públicos.

en.text: Leo XIII's 1896 encyclical to the bishops of Hungary, marking the thousandth anniversary of the Magyar settlement that founded the nation. Recalling the country's conversion under Prince Géza and St. Stephen, the royal crown sent by Sylvester II, and the Church's aid through crises — Innocent XI at Vienna and Buda, Gregory XIII's Roman college — it exhorts Hungarians to renewed Catholic fidelity amid the age's growing religious indifference.

Leo XIII's response to the bishops of Peru after their provincial synod, commending their zeal and setting out four priorities for their pastoral work: seminary education grounded in Thomistic philosophy, careful selection of parish priests, missionary outreach to unconverted peoples, and a Catholic press to counter false opinions. Invokes Saints Turibius and Rose of Lima as patrons of the country.

Pius XII's encyclical marking the 300th anniversary of the martyrdom of St. Andrew Bobola, recounting his birth, Jesuit formation, and zealous pastoral work reconciling schismatics to the Catholic faith in Poland and Lithuania, his torture and death at the hands of Cossacks, and his later beatification and canonization, held up as an example of Christian fortitude to Poland.

Written for the thirteenth centenary of the death of St Gregory the Great, holding up his pastoral government — restoring faith and discipline while Rome collapsed around him — as the pattern for an age in crisis of unbelief. Pius X traces how rationalism and a misapplied critical science wear faith away, insists that only a return to Christ can save society, and asks for careful formation of candidates for the priesthood.

Leo XIII's annual October encyclical urging renewed devotion to the Rosary as the Church's chief recourse amid the tribulations afflicting her liberty and rights. It traces Mary's role as mediatrix through the Joyful and Sorrowful mysteries, then denounces recent blasphemous theatrical mockery of Christ in Italy and calls Catholics to prayer and reparation.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Leão XIII, mais uma das suas exortações anuais ao Rosário mariano no mês de Outubro. Percorre os mistérios gozosos, dolorosos e gloriosos e a oração vocal para mostrar como o Rosário funda a confiança em Maria, Mediadora da graça divina, e termina exortando os fiéis a intensificá-lo diante da perseguição moderna contra a Igreja e dos ultrajes públicos contra a pessoa de Cristo.

en.text: On human work as a fundamental dimension of man's existence, ninety years after Rerum Novarum. It separates work's objective sense — technology, the thing made — from its subjective sense, the person working, argues from that the priority of labour over capital, sets out the rights it founds in wages, unions, disabled and migrant workers, and closes on a spirituality of work drawn from Genesis and from Christ, himself a man of work.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de João Paulo II, publicada no nonagésimo aniversário da Rerum Novarum, sobre o trabalho humano como dimensão fundamental da existência do homem. Distingue o sentido objectivo e subjectivo do trabalho, afirma a prioridade do trabalho sobre o capital face ao conflito moderno entre ambos, enumera os direitos dos trabalhadores — emprego, salário, sindicatos — e conclui com uma espiritualidade do trabalho centrada em Cristo, o homem do trabalho.

en.text: Pius X's 1912 letter to the bishops of Latin America denouncing the continued enslavement, branding, massacre and trafficking of South American Indians despite slavery's formal abolition, and attributing the cruelty to greed and to remoteness from civil and religious oversight. He asks the bishops to sustain the Indian missions by preaching, alms and prayer, and renews Benedict XIV's condemnation of the trade.

Pius XII's 1956 follow-up to his earlier appeal for prayer, giving thanks that Cardinals Wyszyński and Mindszenty have been freed and restored to their sees in Poland and Hungary, and renewing his call for prayers for peace as war threatens in the Middle East.

Leo XIII commends devotion to the Rosary as a remedy for three evils weakening society: distaste for simple, laborious living, met by the Joyful Mysteries; repugnance to suffering, met by the Sorrowful Mysteries; and forgetfulness of the life to come, met by the Glorious Mysteries. He closes by praising the Confraternities of the Rosary and urging bishops to foster the devotion.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Leão XIII sobre o Rosário de Nossa Senhora, escrita para o mês de outubro. Aponta três males da sociedade do seu tempo — a aversão à vida simples, a fuga ao sofrimento e o esquecimento dos bens eternos — e propõe como remédio a meditação dos mistérios gozosos, dolorosos e gloriosos, recomendando ainda a inscrição nas confrarias do Rosário.

en.text: Francis's encyclical on ecology, taking its title from Saint Francis's Canticle of the Creatures. It diagnoses pollution, climate change, water scarcity, biodiversity loss and social breakdown as symptoms of one crisis rooted in a 'technocratic paradigm,' develops an 'integral ecology' linking care for nature to justice for the poor, and proposes lines of dialogue, education, and 'ecological conversion.'

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Francisco, dirigida a cada pessoa que habita este planeta, sobre o cuidado da casa comum. Parte do diagnóstico do que está a acontecer à Terra — poluição, mudanças climáticas, perda de biodiversidade, desigualdade — para propor uma ecologia integral que una a questão ambiental à justiça social, recusando o paradigma tecnocrático e convidando à conversão ecológica; termina com duas orações.

en.text: Pius XII's 1957 letter to the bishops of France marking the centenary of the apparitions at Lourdes, recalling Mary's appearances to Bernadette and her threefold call to penance. Reading the pilgrimage's crowds and its sick as a rebuke to a self-satisfied, materialist age, it urges conversion of heart as the one foundation on which any lasting social or political peace can be built.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Pio XII ao episcopado da França, por ocasião do centenário das aparições de Nossa Senhora em Lourdes. Situa Lourdes na tradição mariana francesa e relembra os laços entre a Santa Sé e o santuário desde Pio IX. Extrai das aparições lições espirituais — conversão pessoal e penitência, renovação cristã da sociedade, predileção de Maria pelos pequenos e enfermos — como programa para o ano jubilar.

en.text: Leo XIII's encyclical on the nature of human liberty, arguing true freedom lies in the will's conformity to the eternal law of God, not in acting simply as one pleases. It examines and limits the liberties liberalism champions — of worship, of speech and the press, of teaching, and of conscience — rejects unconditional separation of Church and State, and allows that Catholics may licitly prefer democratic government.

Leo XIII's encyclical to the Belgian bishops on preserving Catholic unity amid disputes over how far Catholic doctrine should govern the forms of civil law and government. He urges charity in controversy, rebukes attacks on fellow Catholics — naming the accusations against Cardinal Deschamps — and directs scholars to follow St. Thomas Aquinas as the model for philosophy and theology, renewing his call for Thomistic teaching at Louvain.

Leo XIII's encyclical to the archbishops and bishops of Brazil, occasioned by the recent enlargement of the country's episcopal hierarchy, on strengthening the clergy and the faithful: forming priests in well-run seminaries, subjecting religious orders to the bishops' authority, and providing the laity with catechesis, Catholic schools and societies, and a Catholic press.

Leo XIII's letter to the bishops of the United States, marking the centenary of Columbus's discovery and the growth of American Catholicism since its first bishop. It commends the Church's freedom under American law but warns against treating the separation of Church and State there as universally desirable, and takes up Catholic education, workers' associations, the Catholic press, and outreach to non-Catholics, Native Americans and African Americans.

Pius XII's brief appeal, issued at the height of the 1956 Hungarian Revolution, urging bishops worldwide and their flocks to unite in prayer for Hungary and the rest of Eastern Europe, then suffering violent repression and religious persecution under atheistic communism. He calls especially on the young to join the entreaty, invokes the Virgin Mary's intercession, and remembers the region's bishops held in prison, custody, or exile.

On faith as the light of Christ by which human life is guided — the encyclical that completes the trilogy on the theological virtues, drafted by Benedict XVI before his resignation and finished by Francis. It follows faith from Abraham and Israel to Christ, examines its bond with truth and with reason, its transmission through the Church's creed and sacraments, and its power to sustain the family, society and those who suffer.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Francisco, que retoma um esboço de Bento XVI e completa a trilogia sobre as virtudes teológicas iniciada com Deus Caritas Est e Spe Salvi. Descreve a fé como luz que guia o caminho humano, de Abraão à plenitude em Cristo, articula fé, verdade e razão, mostra a Igreja como mãe da fé pelos sacramentos, e trata da fé no bem comum, na família e no sofrimento.

it.text: Enciclica di Pio XI per il XV centenario del Concilio di Efeso, che proclamò la maternità divina di Maria. Ripercorre la condanna dell'eresia di Nestorio e il ruolo decisivo di Celestino I nel confermare, prima ancora del Concilio, l'unità della persona divina in Cristo; ne trae il dogma della Theotókos e propone la Sacra Famiglia di Nazareth come modello per le famiglie cristiane.

en.text: Leo XIII again calls the faithful to devote October to the Rosary of Mary, urging it as a remedy for an age of irreligious schooling, license of press and speech, and insult to Christ. He presents the Rosary as prayer joined to Christian living, a means of meditating the faith's chief mysteries with Mary as model of virtue, and renews the indulgences granted for its recitation.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Leão XIII sobre o Rosário de Nossa Senhora, exortando os fiéis a praticá-lo com fervor redobrado no mês de outubro como remédio contra a incredulidade e a corrupção dos costumes do tempo. Recorda a vitória histórica do Rosário sobre os albigenses, propõe os seus mistérios como exemplo de vida cristã e da Sagrada Família, e liga a exortação ao próprio jubileu episcopal do papa, renovando as indulgências concedidas à prática.

en.text: Leo XIII's 1889 letter approving the statutes of the newly founded Catholic University of America in Washington, D.C. It grants the university the right to confer academic degrees, including in philosophy, theology and canon law, names the Archbishop of Baltimore its chancellor, requires its course of studies be submitted to Rome for approval, and asks that no similar university be established without consulting the Holy See.

ar.text: رسالة بابويّة عامّة للبابا لاوُن الرّابع عشر (2026)، تتناول تعليم الكنيسة الاجتماعيّ في مواجهة تحوّلات الثّورة الرّقميّة والذّكاء الاصطناعيّ. تستعرض أسس هذا التّعليم ومبادئه منذ لاوُن الثّالث عشر، ثمّ تتوقّف عند وعود الذّكاء الاصطناعيّ ومخاطره على الحقيقة والعمل والحرّيّة، وتدعو، في مواجهة ”ثقافة القوّة“ والحروب الجديدة، إلى بناء ”حضارة المحبّة“ المتجذّرة في سرّ التّجسّد.

de.text: Zum 135. Jahrestag von Rerum novarum entwickelt der Text die Soziallehre der Kirche für das Zeitalter der Künstlichen Intelligenz weiter: die Grundprinzipien Gemeinwohl, allgemeine Bestimmung der Güter, Subsidiarität, Solidarität und soziale Gerechtigkeit, dann Wahrheit, Arbeit und Freiheit im digitalen Wandel sowie Krieg, KI-Waffen und die Kultur der Macht, der die Zivilisation der Liebe entgegengesetzt wird; er schließt mit einem marianischen Aufruf zu Gebet und Hoffnung.

en.text: Leo XIV's encyclical on artificial intelligence and the social doctrine of the Church. Framed by two biblical images of collective building — the Tower of Babel and Nehemiah's rebuilding of Jerusalem — it argues that AI is not one more subject for social doctrine to address but a development that challenges its categories from within, and takes up human dignity and the common good, truth, work and freedom, and the growing place of autonomous systems in war.

es.text: Carta encíclica de León XIV sobre la custodia de la persona humana en el tiempo de la inteligencia artificial. Enmarcada por dos imágenes bíblicas de construcción colectiva —la torre de Babel y la reconstrucción de Jerusalén por Nehemías—, sostiene que la IA no es un tema añadido a la Doctrina social sino una transformación que interpela sus categorías desde dentro, y trata la dignidad humana, la verdad, el trabajo, la libertad y el lugar creciente de los sistemas autónomos en la guerra.

fr.text: Sur la protection de la personne humaine à l'ère de l'intelligence artificielle. En cinq chapitres, l'encyclique retrace l'évolution de la Doctrine sociale de l'Église depuis Léon XIII, en expose les fondements — dignité, bien commun, subsidiarité, solidarité —, puis examine les répercussions du numérique sur la vérité, le travail et la liberté, la banalisation de la guerre, et appelle à bâtir la civilisation de l'amour.

it.text: Lettera enciclica di Leone XIV sulla custodia della persona umana nel tempo dell’intelligenza artificiale. Incorniciata dalle icone bibliche della torre di Babele e della ricostruzione di Gerusalemme guidata da Neemia, sostiene che l’IA non è un tema aggiuntivo per la Dottrina sociale ma una trasformazione che ne interpella le categorie, e tratta la dignità umana, la verità, il lavoro, la libertà e il posto dei sistemi autonomi in guerra.

pl.text: Encyklika Leona XIV o trosce o osobę ludzką w dobie sztucznej inteligencji. Osadzając to zagadnienie w rozwoju nauki społecznej Kościoła od Leona XIII po dziś, omawia godność osoby ludzkiej, zasady dobra wspólnego, pomocniczości i solidarności wobec przemiany cyfrowej, godność pracy i wolność zagrożoną uzależnieniem, oraz niebezpieczeństwo wojny prowadzonej przy użyciu sztucznej inteligencji, wzywając do budowania „cywilizacji miłości” w miejsce „kultury potęgi”.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Leão XIV sobre a inteligência artificial e a doutrina social da Igreja. Estruturada em torno de duas imagens bíblicas da construção comum — a Torre de Babel e a reconstrução de Jerusalém por Neemias —, sustenta que a IA não é mais um tema a tratar pela doutrina social, mas um desenvolvimento que desafia as suas próprias categorias, e aborda a dignidade humana e o bem comum, a verdade, o trabalho e a liberdade, e o lugar crescente dos sistemas autónomos na guerra.

ru.text: Энциклика Льва XIV о защите человеческой личности в эпоху искусственного интеллекта. Опираясь на историю социального учения Церкви от Льва XIII до наших дней и на его принципы — общее благо, субсидиарность, солидарность, — она рассматривает вызовы ИИ для истины, труда, свободы и семьи, критикует трансгуманизм и культуру мощи и призывает созидать цивилизацию любви.

en.text: John XXIII's restatement of Catholic social teaching on the seventieth anniversary of Rerum Novarum, carrying Leo XIII's principles forward through Quadragesimo Anno and Pius XII's radio addresses. It then takes up newer aspects of the social question — the depressed state of agriculture, the gap between developed and developing nations, population growth, and international cooperation — and closes with principles for rebuilding a social order on truth, justice, and love.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de João XXIII, setenta anos após a Rerum Novarum, sobre a recente evolução da questão social à luz da doutrina cristã. Retoma os ensinamentos de Leão XIII, Pio XI e Pio XII sobre socialização, salário e propriedade privada, trata novos aspectos — agricultura, desigualdade entre nações e crescimento demográfico — e conclui com um apelo à renovação das relações humanas na verdade, na justiça e no amor.

en.text: Settles the question of the Diocesan Associations, left open in France since the separation law of 1905. Reviewing the associations cultuelles that Pius X had condemned, Pius XI approves new statutes negotiated with the French government and examined by canonists and the Council of State, permits the dioceses to form associations under them, and repeats his predecessor's condemnation of the Lay Laws.

The sacred liturgy as the public worship that the Church, united with Christ her divine Head, offers to God: the priesthood's role in the Eucharistic sacrifice, the laity's active yet real participation in it, the sacraments and sacramentals, the Divine Office and liturgical year, and pastoral counsel on sacred art, music and altar servers, warning against both careless innovation and an exaggerated antiquarian zeal for reviving ancient forms.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Pio XII sobre a sagrada liturgia: trata da sua natureza como culto público e hierárquico da Igreja, do sacrifício eucarístico e da participação dos fiéis nele, da comunhão e adoração eucarísticas, do ofício divino e do ciclo do ano litúrgico, e encerra com diretrizes pastorais sobre outras formas de piedade e o espírito litúrgico a fomentar entre clero e povo.

en.text: Pius XII's encyclical calling the Church to renewed prayer, especially through the intercession of the Virgin Mary, for Christians suffering persecution under regimes that deny the Church's rights, including dioceses left without a lawful bishop. It urges the faithful to join public prayer with a genuine renewal of Christian life, so that religious liberty and communion with the Holy See may be restored to persecuted peoples.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Pio XII (1958) que convoca orações públicas pela paz do mundo e a liberdade da Igreja, na novena da Assunção. Descreve as perseguições sofridas pela Igreja católica, de rito latino e oriental, na Europa e na Ásia oriental — imprensa e escolas suprimidas, missionários expulsos — e exorta à renovação cristã dos costumes unida à oração, confiando esses votos à Virgem Maria.

en.text: Pius XI, on the golden jubilee of his ordination, urges wider practice of the Spiritual Exercises — retreats modeled on Christ's own withdrawals to the desert — as a remedy for the thoughtlessness of the age. He commends St. Ignatius of Loyola's method as foremost, presses their use among clergy, religious, laity and Catholic Action, and recommends a monthly day of recollection to preserve their fruit.

Paul VI asks that the month of May be given to prayer to Mary for two urgent reasons: the Second Vatican Council, still sitting, and a peace in jeopardy as international tensions worsen. He condemns the disregard for human life that armed conflict brings, appeals to the world's rulers to renounce force, and asks children and the suffering in particular to pray the Rosary for peace.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Paulo VI, publicada às vésperas do mês mariano de maio de 1965, convocando os fiéis à oração — especialmente ao Rosário — por duas intenções: o bom êxito da última sessão do Concílio Vaticano II e a paz mundial, ameaçada por conflitos armados, guerrilhas e atos de terrorismo. Termina confiando ambas as causas à intercessão de Maria, Rainha da paz.

en.text: Leo XIII's encyclical marking the third centenary of St. Peter Canisius's death, addressed to the bishops of Austria, Germany and Switzerland. It holds up Canisius, second apostle of Germany after Boniface, as a model of uniting sound learning with the defense of the faith against the Reformation, and urges Catholic schools, the union of piety with study, and unity among Catholics.

Pius XII's encyclical calling Catholics to a crusade of prayer for world peace, urging public supplications, an Immaculate Conception midnight Mass broadcast by radio, and prayers through the Christmas novena, invoking Mary's intercession against the era's wars, hatreds and persecution of the Church.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Pio XII, escrita em meio a temores de um novo conflito mundial, pedindo aos bispos orações públicas pela paz e pela concórdia entre os povos, com súplicas especiais na véspera da festa da Imaculada Conceição e durante a novena do Natal.

en.text: Leo XIII's encyclical on the Holy Eucharist, issued for the twenty-fifth anniversary of his pontificate. It presents the Eucharist as the source of the Church's supernatural life and the strengthening of faith, then as the bond of charity that remedies the social divisions of the age, and closes on the Eucharistic sacrifice of the Mass and its daily fruits for the world.
