Pius XII's encyclical on the motion picture, radio and television industries, extending Vigilanti Cura's principles on film to broadcasting. It explains why these arts concern the Church, sets out the freedoms and duties of directors, distributors, actors and public authorities, and gives bishops detailed instructions for guiding Catholics, including parents, clergy and national offices, toward their right use.

pt.text: Trata o cinema, a rádio e a televisão como dons providenciais de difusão que podem servir tanto o bem como o mal, e expõe a doutrina cristã sobre a liberdade de difusão perante o Estado e o público. Detalha deveres de produtores, actores, exibidores, radiouvintes e telespectadores, e termina com uma exortação ao clero para acompanhar pastoralmente estas técnicas modernas.

en.text: Pius XI's encyclical on reparation to the Sacred Heart of Jesus, presented as completing the consecration he had established through Quas Primas and the feast of Christ the King. It grounds the duty of expiatory reparation in Christ's continuing sufferings within his Mystical Body, laments the era's apostasy and ingratitude toward the Sacred Heart, and decrees an annual Act of Reparation to be recited in every church.

Pius XI's 1937 encyclical to the archbishops and bishops of Germany, addressing the persecution of the Church under the Reich government. It recalls the Church's 1933 concordat with Germany and catalogs its violation, condemns the elevation of race, people, or state to a divinized absolute in place of God, and reaffirms revelation, the natural law, and the Church's right to freedom and to defend the faithful.

Pius XI on the interwar movement to reunite separated Christian bodies through shared conferences and mutual charity without doctrinal agreement. The encyclical rejects this “pan-Christian” approach, holding that Christ's prayer that his followers be one is already fulfilled in the visible, doctrinally united Catholic Church, forbids Catholic participation in such assemblies, and insists that reunion comes only through return to the one true Church under the Bishop of Rome.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Pio XI aos bispos católicos sobre a unidade verdadeira da religião, contra o movimento "pancristão" e seus congressos ecumênicos, que buscam uma fraternidade comum ignorando as diferenças doutrinárias. Pio XI ensina que só existe uma religião verdadeira, revelada por Deus e guardada pela Igreja Católica, e que a unidade dos cristãos só se dá pelo retorno dos dissidentes a essa única Igreja, em obediência ao Romano Pontífice.

en.text: Pius XII's encyclical on sacred music, tracing its history from the early Church through Gregorian chant and polyphony and setting out the principles by which sacred music must be holy, artistic, and universal. It defends Gregorian chant's primacy while approving polyphony, the organ, and vernacular hymns, addresses missionary lands, and recommends choirs, seminary training, and diocesan councils of sacred art to bishops.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Pio XII sobre a música sacra na liturgia. Traça a sua história desde o Antigo Testamento até ao canto gregoriano e à polifonia, expõe os princípios que regem a arte religiosa, distingue a música litúrgica da religiosa e da popular, e trata do uso do latim, do órgão e de outros instrumentos, com recomendações aos bispos para promover coros, seminários e conselhos diocesanos de arte sacra.

en.text: Mysterium Fidei, on the Holy Eucharist, written while the Council was still sitting to check opinions then circulating that would reduce the Real Presence to symbolism or put transignification in the place of transubstantiation. It reaffirms the Mass as both sacrifice and sacrament, defends Trent's language on Christ's substantial presence and the adoration due the Sacrament, and closes urging daily Mass and Eucharistic devotion.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Paulo VI sobre o culto da Sagrada Eucaristia, escrita para corrigir opiniões que confundiam os fiéis quanto à Missa, à transubstanciação e ao culto eucarístico. Reafirma a doutrina de Trento sobre o Sacrifício da Missa e a presença real de Cristo pela transubstanciação, defende a linguagem tradicional da fé e exorta à adoração do Santíssimo Sacramento reservado e exposto à veneração dos fiéis.

en.text: On the Church as the Mystical Body of Christ: a single visible Body with Christ as Head, animated by the Holy Spirit and built up through the sacraments and the juridical bonds of faith, hope and charity. It refutes rationalist, naturalist and mystical errors about the Church's nature and closes by entrusting her peace to the Virgin Mary.

pt.text: Sobre o Corpo Místico de Cristo, que é a Igreja: define-a como um corpo único, visível e organicamente estruturado, cuja cabeça é Cristo e cujo vigário visível é o Papa, vivificada interiormente pelo Espírito Santo e unida pelos sacramentos, sobretudo a Eucaristia. Denuncia os erros do falso misticismo e do quietismo, exorta à caridade ativa para com a Igreja e encerra confiando os fiéis à Virgem Maria.

en.text: Leo XIII to the bishops of France on the anti-clerical measures then underway, the suppression of religious orders and the secularizing laws. He urges the French, “eldest daughter of the Church”, to keep religious instruction within the family, to respect the distinct but harmonious authority of Church and State, to preserve unity among Catholics under their bishops, and to answer persecution with prayer and constancy.

Pius XI's protest against the Fascist government's 1931 suppression of Catholic Action's youth and university associations in Italy. He defends Catholic Action as lay collaboration with the bishops, not politics, rejects charges that it serves a 'foreign power,' and insists that the Christian education of youth belongs to the Church by divine mandate, not to a state claiming exclusive command over the young.

Leo XIII's 1893 letter to the bishops of Spain announcing the foundation of a Roman college for Spanish clerics. Recalling Spain's earlier renown for theological and literary learning, he laments how seminaries and universities were uprooted by the upheavals following the French Revolution, and establishes a Roman residence for Spanish students, in a building once belonging to the Dukes of Altemps, under the oversight of the Archbishops of Toledo and Seville.

Pius XI writes to Mexico's bishops during the country's anti-Catholic persecution, praising the fidelity of clergy and faithful and urging two remedies: holier priests, and lay Catholic Action organized to reach workers, peasants and indigenous Mexicans, students, and emigrants to the United States. It calls for pursuing social justice without violent upheaval, for civic engagement including voting, and entrusts Mexico to Our Lady of Guadalupe.

Pius XI's brief appeal amid the Great Depression on the unemployment and want afflicting workers and, above all, their children. He calls the Church to a 'Crusade of charity' — alms and prayer gathered through the bishops — to relieve the destitute, and asks that solemn tridua be held before the feast of Christ the King to implore peace from the God of Mercies.

Leo XIII's annual encyclical urging the faithful to pray the Rosary throughout October, recommending it as Mary's own weapon against the Church's enemies — recalling how Saint Dominic used it against the Albigensian heresy — and calling for prayer joined to penance, so that intercession through the Mother of God might win the Church's deliverance from persecution and error.

pt.text: Encíclica de Leão XIII que renova o convite anual à oração do mês de Outubro, recomendando o Santo Rosário como a forma de recorrer a Maria, medianeira de todas as graças, contra os males que afligem a Igreja. Recorda a origem do Rosário por São Domingos e une à oração a exortação à mortificação e à penitência, com esperança nos frutos da intercessão da Rainha do Rosário.

en.text: Leo XIII's 1887 encyclical to the archbishops and bishops of Bavaria, recalling the region's Catholic history from Severinus and St. Boniface and urging renewed care for the training of clergy, grounded in Thomistic philosophy and theology, against rationalist error and Freemasonry. It reviews the concordat between the Holy See and Bavaria and calls for vigilance in defending the Church's rights and liberty.

Pius XII on the social unrest that followed the Second World War: economic ruin has left workers idle while agitators incite class hatred and rioting in place of relief. Rejecting both rancor and the pursuit of private profit as remedies, he calls for reconciliation through Christian charity and prescribes public prayers — especially by children at the Christmas crib — for peace and for the relief of the needy.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Pio XII, de 18 de dezembro de 1947, convocando orações públicas pelo restabelecimento da paz social e mundial após a guerra, exortando à concórdia entre nações e classes sociais e pedindo especialmente as orações das crianças no Natal, com esmolas e obras de piedade, para aplacar a justiça divina.

en.text: Pius XII's encyclical marking the 350th anniversary of the Union of Brest, by which the Ruthenian Church entered communion with Rome. It traces that reunion's history — the negotiations of 1595–96, the martyrdom of Josaphat Kuntsevych, and Rome's steady defense of the Ruthenian rite against Latinization — before turning to the persecution then engulfing the Ruthenian Church and exhorting its bishops, priests, and faithful to constancy.

For the fifteenth centenary of St Cyril of Alexandria, recounting his defence of the unity of Christ's person against Nestorius, his deference to the Apostolic See through the Council of Ephesus, and his patient reconciliation with the Antiochene bishops — which Pius XII holds up as the model for reunion with the separated Christians of the East, the modern Nestorians and those who do not receive Chalcedon.

On charity and mutual pardon between men and between nations, written weeks after the peace treaties that ended the First World War. Benedict XV presses for the forgiving of wartime enmities, commends practical relief for the widows, the orphans and the devastated regions, and calls the states to unite in a league — a family of peoples — to reduce armaments and keep the peace.

John XXIII grounds peace in an order willed by God, traced through four relations: the rights and duties of the individual person; citizens and the public authority over them; states with one another, owed truth, justice, solidarity and an end to the arms race; and political communities with a still-forming world community, whose own public authority he sees the United Nations beginning to supply.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de João XXIII (1963) sobre a paz entre todos os povos, fundada na verdade, na justiça, na caridade e na liberdade. Expõe direitos e deveres da pessoa humana, a origem e função da autoridade nos poderes públicos, as relações entre comunidades políticas e destas com a comunidade mundial, e conclui com diretrizes pastorais para a ação dos católicos na vida pública.

en.text: John XXIII's call to the whole Church, clergy and laity alike, for prayer and penance in preparation for the Second Vatican Council, invoking Scripture's repeated calls to penance and the precedent of earlier councils. It urges a solemn novena to the Holy Spirit carrying a plenary indulgence, and distinguishes internal repentance — confession and the Eucharist — from the voluntary external acts of penance offered for the Council's success.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de João XXIII (1962) que convoca todo o povo cristão — bispos, clero e fiéis — à penitência interior e exterior, à oração e à mortificação voluntária como preparação espiritual para o Concílio Ecumênico Vaticano II. Percorre os apelos bíblicos e patrísticos à penitência para pedir um renovado fervor de fé e de vida cristã, de modo que o Concílio produza os frutos de unidade e renovação que dele se esperam.

en.text: Pius X's systematic condemnation of Modernism as “the synthesis of all heresies,” set out through the several roles a Modernist combines — philosopher, believer, theologian, historian and critic, apologist, reformer — and tracing agnosticism and “vital immanence” through his account of dogma, Scripture, and the Church. It then prescribes remedies: scholastic philosophy in seminaries, censorship of publications, and diocesan vigilance councils reporting to Rome every three years.

Leo XIII's 1891 encyclical to the bishops of Germany and Austria-Hungary condemning dueling as a violation of divine and natural law. He reviews the Church's traditional penalties against duelists, refutes the excuses offered for the practice — that it vindicates injured honor, or that refusing a challenge invites the charge of cowardice — and rejects any exemption claimed for the military.

Leo XIII writes to the cardinals and bishops of Portugal following the Catholic Congress of Braga, urging annual episcopal conferences alongside the lay congresses, closer union among bishops, and diocesan and provincial synods leading toward a national council. He commends founding religious societies to train clergy and supply missionaries for Portugal's overseas territories, and restates that the Church strengthens rather than weakens civil authority.

Leo XIII's encyclical to the bishops, clergy, and people of the Armenian Rite, welcoming the recent return of part of that community to communion with Rome and urging its consolidation. He exhorts the bishops to draw the still-separated Armenians back as well, recalling their nation's historical fidelity to the Holy See — from Gregory the Illuminator through the Council of Florence — and closes invoking the intercession of Our Lady and St. Gregory.

An appeal for the starving and destitute children of central Europe after the First World War. Benedict XV commends the Save the Children societies formed to help them, directs bishops to order public prayers and to gather alms, food, medicine and clothing on the feast of the Holy Innocents, and pledges a hundred thousand lire of his own toward the relief.

Pius X's admonition to the Italian bishops against a spirit of insubordination and independence spreading among the younger clergy. It demands strict seminary discipline, regulates who may preach and publish, reaffirms earlier norms governing “Popular Christian Action”, and forbids clerics from joining any society lacking episcopal approval, naming the National Democratic League specifically.

Paul VI's encyclical on the development of peoples, arguing that authentic development must be integral — of the whole man and of every man — and tracing the passage from less than human to more human conditions. It sets out the wealthier nations' threefold duty toward developing ones — solidarity, social justice and universal charity — and closes on development as the new name for peace.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Paulo VI sobre o desenvolvimento dos povos, defendendo um desenvolvimento integral — do homem todo e de todos os homens — e a passagem de condições menos humanas, marcadas pela miséria e pela opressão, a condições mais humanas. Aponta o tríplice dever das nações ricas para com as mais pobres — solidariedade, justiça social e caridade universal — e conclui que o desenvolvimento é o novo nome da paz.

en.text: Princeps Pastorum, on the missions forty years after Benedict XV's Maximum Illud. John XXIII treats the formation of a native clergy — local hierarchies, seminaries that form men in holiness, a missiology fitted to the mind of each people while guarding unity against ultranationalism — then the apostolate of the laity through Catholic Action, catechists and the Christian school, closing with an appeal for vocations and for perseverance under persecution.

Benedict XV's encyclical proclaiming St. Ephrem the Syrian, deacon of Edessa, a Doctor of the Universal Church, with his feast fixed on 18 June. A companion to his encyclical on St. Jerome, it recounts Ephrem's life, teaching and hymnody — “the lyre of the Holy Spirit” — his devotion to the Virgin and to Peter's primacy, and appeals for the reunion of the separated Eastern churches with Rome.

Leo XIII's encyclical on the study of Holy Scripture, addressed to the bishops of the Catholic world. It commends Scripture's benefits, traces the Church's guardianship of the biblical text, and gives detailed instructions for teaching it in seminaries. Much of the letter defends the Bible's authority against rationalist criticism and physical science, insisting that divine inspiration excludes all error from the sacred writings.

Pius XI's encyclical for the fortieth anniversary of Leo XIII's On the Condition of Workers, treated under three headings: that encyclical's fruits, Catholic teaching on property's individual and social character and on just wages, and a verdict on the present economic order — wealth concentrated into an “economic dictatorship,” free competition's self-destruction, and Socialism's irreconcilability with Christianity — closing with a call to restore society through vocational guilds and reform of morals.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Pio XI no quadragésimo aniversário da Rerum Novarum: reafirma o direito de propriedade e a justiça do salário, propõe corporações profissionais que reúnam patrões e operários para restaurar a ordem social, e examina as mudanças na economia — o despotismo económico do capitalismo — e no socialismo, incompatível com o catolicismo. Termina apelando à reforma cristã dos costumes, pela justiça e caridade sociais.

en.text: A brief pastoral letter to the Archbishop of Prague and the bishops of Bohemia and Moravia, prompted by growing defections from Catholic rites and practice in their dioceses. Leo XIII urges the bishops to hold a joint meeting, its resolutions subject to papal approval, to coordinate a common defense of the faith, and to root out the partisan rivalries splitting their own clergy that weaken the unity such a defense requires.

Leo XIII's letter to the bishops of America on the spiritual and material hardships facing Italian emigrants, who often lack priests able to minister to them in their own language. He announces the Apostolic College of Priests he founded at Piacenza to train clergy for their pastoral care, asks the bishops to receive its graduates, and urges itinerant missions where Italians are most numerous.

On the kingship of Christ over persons, families and states, gathering the scriptural, patristic and liturgical evidence for a dominion the age's anticlericalism had set out to deny. Closing the Holy Year of 1925, it institutes the feast of Christ the King on the last Sunday of October and joins to it the yearly renewal of the consecration of mankind to the Sacred Heart.

Pius XII's post-war appeal to the bishops on behalf of the world's destitute children, millions of whom the conflict left without food, shelter, clothing, or care. He asks that a day of public prayer be set aside in every diocese and urges the faithful to support relief through prayer, almsgiving, and organized charitable works, warning that neglect now will breed sickness, vice, and delinquency in the next generation.

pt.text: Encíclica de Pio XII sobre a assistência às crianças indigentes no pós-guerra. Descreve a multidão de crianças órfãs, famintas e sem-teto deixadas pelo conflito mundial, recorda o cuidado constante da Igreja pela infância desde Cristo e apela aos bispos e fiéis para que redobrem a caridade e criem novas iniciativas em seu socorro.

en.text: Leo XIII's encyclical for his sacerdotal jubilee, the fiftieth anniversary of his ordination, giving thanks for the celebrations and recent canonizations and beatifications, and marking the occasion by decreeing the last Sunday of September 1888 as a day of solemn Mass for the dead throughout the Church, with a plenary indulgence for the relief of souls in purgatory.

On socialism, communism and nihilism, whose rise Leo XIII traces to the sixteenth-century revolt against the Catholic faith and to the philosophers' doctrine of unbridled liberty. It defends legitimate civil authority, the indissolubility of marriage and the family, and the natural right of private property against claims of absolute equality and common ownership, and asks bishops to keep workingmen out of the sect.

Leo XIII's encyclical proclaiming an extraordinary Jubilee for 1886, urging the faithful to penance, prayer and devotion to the Rosary amid moral decline and dissension among the clergy, then granting a plenary indulgence on stated conditions — church visits, fasting, confession, Communion and almsgiving toward parish schools and seminaries — for Rome's citizens, the wider world, sailors and travellers alike.

Written three weeks after the Armistice, with the peace congress about to meet: Benedict XV asks the bishops to order public prayers in every parish for its success, that what the delegates decide may rest on the Christian principles of justice and secure a true and lasting peace.

Leo XIII's encyclical to the bishops of Hungary, written for the bicentenary of Budapest's liberation from Turkish rule, recalling St. Stephen and the nation's historic bond with the Holy See. It warns against rationalism and socialism, and gives directives on defending the Church's liberty, upholding Catholic marriage, forming Catholic youth, and supporting seminaries and the clergy's pastoral work.

Leo XIII writes to the Archbishops and Bishops of Austria — of Vienna, Wroclaw, Prague, and Krakow — approving their long-pending plan to found a Catholic university. He expresses joy that the project, awaited under his predecessors, is nearing completion, urges the faithful to hasten it, and directs that its final arrangements be reported to the Sacred Congregation of Studies for approval under canonical norms.

John Paul II's first encyclical, opening his pontificate on the claim that Jesus Christ, the Redeemer of man, is the centre of the universe and of history. Taking up the inheritance of Vatican II, it turns to the man Redemption reaches — afraid of what his own progress has made, his rights honoured in letter or in spirit — and to the Church's answer in truth, in the Eucharist and Penance, and in service.

pt.text: Primeira encíclica de João Paulo II, que abre o seu pontificado situando Cristo Redentor como centro do cosmos e da história. Em quatro partes, recolhe a herança do Concílio Vaticano II, expõe as dimensões divina e humana da Redenção, examina a situação do homem contemporâneo entre progresso e ameaça aos seus direitos, e conclui sobre a missão da Igreja ao serviço da verdade e da vocação real dos cristãos.

en.text: John Paul II's encyclical on the Blessed Virgin Mary in the life of the pilgrim Church, proclaiming a Marian Year before the third millennium. It follows Mary's pilgrimage of faith in three parts: her place in the mystery of Christ, from the Annunciation to “Behold your mother” at the Cross; her role at the center of the Church's journey toward Christian unity; and her maternal mediation, subordinate to Christ's one mediation.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de João Paulo II sobre a Bem-Aventurada Virgem Maria na vida da Igreja que está a caminho, escrita para anunciar um Ano Mariano antes do fim do segundo milénio. Percorre, em três partes, a presença de Maria no mistério de Cristo, o seu lugar no centro da Igreja peregrina e a sua mediação materna, sempre subordinada à única mediação de Cristo.

en.text: John Paul II reasserts the permanent validity of the Church's mandate to bring the Gospel to every people, twenty-five years after the Council's Ad Gentes and against currents that would narrow it. He grounds mission in Christ the one Savior, the Kingdom of God, and the Holy Spirit as its principal agent, then traces its paths — witness, proclamation, conversion, inculturation, dialogue, human development — closing on missionary spirituality.

Pius XII's encyclical on the Holy Places of Palestine in the aftermath of the 1948 war, appealing on behalf of refugees driven from their homes and for an internationally guaranteed status for Jerusalem and the sacred sites damaged by the fighting. It urges continued relief for exiles, protection and free pilgrim access to the Holy Places, and a just and lasting peace.

Pius XI on the Catholic missions, setting two aims: more and better-trained missionaries, and lay Catholics who pray and give for them through the Society for the Propagation of the Faith. Its sharpest passage takes up Benedict XV's complaint that ancient mission territories still have no native bishops, and it commits the Pope to redividing and reassigning mission territories — to native clergy where possible — rather than leaving them to the institute that opened them.

es.text: Pío XI sobre las misiones católicas, con dos objetivos: más misioneros y mejor formados, y laicos que recen y contribuyan a ellos por medio de la Obra de la Propagación de la Fe. Su pasaje más incisivo retoma la queja de Benedicto XV de que territorios de misión antiguos siguen sin obispos autóctonos, y compromete al Papa a dividir y reasignar territorios de misión —al clero autóctono siempre que sea posible— en lugar de dejarlos al instituto que los abrió.

fr.text: Pie XI sur les missions catholiques, avec deux objectifs : davantage de missionnaires et mieux formés, et des laïcs qui prient et donnent pour eux par l'Œuvre de la Propagation de la Foi. Son passage le plus incisif reprend la plainte de Benoît XV selon laquelle d'anciens territoires de mission n'ont toujours pas d'évêques autochtones, et il engage le Pape à diviser et à réattribuer les territoires de mission — au clergé autochtone lorsque c'est possible — plutôt que de les laisser à l'institut qui les a ouverts.

it.text: Pio XI sulle missioni cattoliche, con due obiettivi: più missionari e meglio formati, e laici che preghino e contribuiscano per loro tramite l'Opera della Propagazione della Fede. Il passaggio più incisivo riprende la lamentela di Benedetto XV che territori di missione antichi siano ancora senza vescovi autoctoni, e impegna il Papa a dividere e riassegnare i territori di missione — al clero autoctono ove possibile — invece di lasciarli all'istituto che li ha aperti.

pt.text: Pio XI sobre as missões católicas, com dois objectivos: mais missionários e melhor formados, e leigos que rezem e contribuam para eles através da Obra da Propagação da Fé. A sua passagem mais incisiva retoma a queixa de Bento XV de que territórios de missão antigos continuam sem bispos autóctones, e compromete o Papa a dividir e reatribuir territórios de missão — ao clero autóctone sempre que possível — em vez de os deixar ao instituto que os abriu.

en.text: On the condition of labor amid industrial upheaval, addressing what the document itself calls the rights and duties of capital and labor. It refutes the socialist proposal to abolish private property, grounds ownership in natural and paternal right, sets out duties binding workers and employers alike, and turns to the roles of Church, State, and workingmen's associations in bettering the workman's condition.

pt.text: Encíclica de Leão XIII, de 1891, sobre a condição dos operários, escrita depois do fim das antigas corporações que os protegiam. Rejeita a solução socialista de abolir a propriedade particular como injusta, defende o direito natural à propriedade e à livre associação dos trabalhadores, e trata dos deveres do Estado, dos patrões e dos operários, incluindo a justa retribuição do trabalho.

en.text: Marks the third centenary of the death of St Francis de Sales, recounting his gentle but resolute holiness, surveying his major writings — the Introduction to the Devout Life, the Treatise on the Love of God, and the Controversies written during his mission to the Chablais — and declaring him heavenly patron of writers.

it.text: Pio XI ripercorre l'impegno secolare della Sede Apostolica per gli studi orientali, dai collegi medievali di Parigi ai predecessori più recenti, per motivare la fondazione del Pontificio Istituto Orientale, affidato ai Gesuiti e trasferito presso Sant'Antonio all'Esquilino. Esorta i Vescovi a formare nei seminari sacerdoti esperti di teologia, liturgia e lingue orientali, in vista del ritorno degli Orientali separati all'unità con Roma.

en.text: Pius XI's encyclical for the seventh centenary of the death of St. Francis of Assisi, describing him as God's providential answer to a medieval society riven by class hostility and moral decay. It surveys Francis's poverty, humility and obedience, the Rule he gave the Friars Minor, and the Second and Third Orders that grew from his reform, urging the world's bishops to promote the Third Order anew for the centenary.

Sacerdotalis Caelibatus, reaffirming the law of priestly celibacy in the Latin Church against the objections — doctrinal, historical, sociological, pastoral — raised after the Council, and grounding it in Christ's own celibacy and the priest's configuration to him. It treats the human dimensions of celibacy, formation in chastity, and dispensation for those who leave the priesthood, closing with an appeal to bishops and laity to sustain their priests.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Paulo VI que reafirma a lei do celibato sacerdotal, respondendo às objeções levantadas após o Concílio Vaticano II. Expõe o significado cristológico, eclesiológico e escatológico do celibato consagrado, trata da formação e da vida espiritual dos sacerdotes, do problema das deserções e dispensas, e convida bispos, sacerdotes e fiéis a sustentar essa vocação.

en.text: Written for the centenary of the death of St John Mary Vianney, holding up the Curé of Ars as the model of a priest: his poverty, chastity and obedience, his life of prayer and his devotion to the Eucharist and the Mass, and his zeal as preacher, catechist and confessor. It closes by asking bishops, the faithful and the young themselves to foster priestly vocations.

Benedict XV's encyclical for the seventh centenary of the Third Order of St. Francis, defending the true character of Francis of Assisi against Modernist reinterpretation and naming fraternal charity as the Tertiaries' distinguishing mark. It addresses the social unrest and class conflict of the age, calls the Third Order to carry the spirit of Christ into social life, and closes by granting indulgences for the centenary's Triduum.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Pio XII sobre a virgindade e a castidade perfeita consagradas a Deus. Expõe a doutrina patrística sobre a excelência da virgindade em relação ao matrimônio, refuta os erros que a dizem nociva ao organismo ou menos santificante e apostólica que o casamento, trata da vigilância, do pudor e da devoção mariana necessários para vivê-la, e exorta a fomentar as vocações religiosas.

en.text: Written to the bishops of Portugal for the eighth centenary of Portuguese independence, recalling how papal protection of the medieval kingdom bound its history to the spread of the faith through its missions. Pius XII asks for renewed recruitment and training of missionaries for the African and Asian territories, invokes Francis Xavier and John de Brito as patrons, and appeals to clergy and Catholic Action to sustain that work.

Leo XIII on the Church's three mission societies — the Propagation of the Faith, the Holy Infancy, and the Schools of the East — recounting the alms and prayers they gather for the missions, the growing shortage of missionaries at a time of persecution abroad and secularizing laws in Europe, and asking bishops, clergy and faithful to sustain the work with prayer, alms and vocations.

Leo XIII's encyclical on the duties of Christians as citizens, addressing the relationship between allegiance to the Church and obedience to civil authority: civil laws contrary to divine law may not be obeyed, the Church is a perfect society independent of the State, parents and laity share responsibility for teaching the faith, and Catholics are urged to defend religion in public life through prudent, courageous action and Christian charity.

Leo XIII's encyclical on the unity of the Church, describing it as one visible society and mystical body founded by Christ, bound by unity of faith under a perpetual teaching Magisterium. It grounds supreme authority in Peter's primacy, inherited jure divino by the Roman Pontiffs, holds bishops united to the Church only while joined to Peter's successors, and appeals to those outside the fold to return.

Written to the American hierarchy for the hundred-and-fiftieth anniversary of its establishment, recalling the growth of the Church in the United States from John Carroll's appointment as its first bishop to its present schools, missions and lay associations. It then warns against materialism in education and the breakdown of marriage, and asks for a just settlement of the labour question.

Settles the German 'trade union controversy': whether Catholic workers, alongside purely Catholic Arbeitervereine, may join mixed interconfessional labor unions with Protestants. Addressed to Cardinal Kopp and the German bishops, it reaffirms Rerum Novarum's principles and permits qualified toleration of the Christian Trade Unions where local conditions warrant, provided members also belong to a Catholic association and the unions never act against Church teaching, under episcopal oversight.

For the eleventh centenary of the death of St Methodius, presenting him with his brother Cyril as the apostles of the Slavs. It follows their lives and their peaceable missionary method — preaching and celebrating the liturgy in the language of the people they came to — and reads them as pioneers of what would later be called inculturation, who bound the Slav peoples into the Church's catholicity and into the common civilization of Christian Europe.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de João Paulo II, publicada para o undécimo centenário da morte de são Metódio, sobre os santos Cirilo e Metódio, apóstolos dos eslavos: suas vidas, o método missionário de traduzir a Escritura e a liturgia para a língua eslava, o sentido católico da Igreja e o alcance do milênio cristão entre os povos eslavos, concluindo com uma oração pela herança da fé eslava.

en.text: A rereading of Paul VI's Populorum Progressio on its twentieth anniversary, surveying how the development of peoples has fared since 1967: East-West bloc rivalry, the arms race, international debt, and unemployment. It diagnoses ‘structures of sin’ behind these failures and proposes solidarity and a preferential love for the poor as the path to authentic human development.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de João Paulo II, publicada no vigésimo aniversário da Populorum Progressio de Paulo VI, que retoma e actualiza o seu ensinamento sobre o desenvolvimento dos povos. Traça um panorama do mundo contemporâneo dividido em blocos e marcado pelo subdesenvolvimento, identifica os «mecanismos perversos» e as «estruturas de pecado» que o entravam, e propõe a solidariedade como virtude moral necessária à verdadeira libertação humana.

en.text: Benedict XVI on Christian hope, beginning from Paul's “in hope we were saved” and asking what kind of hope could make that true. It reads hope in the New Testament and the early Church, traces its modern replacement by faith in progress — from Bacon to the French and Marxist revolutions — and argues that progress builds no lasting kingdom. It then offers three settings in which hope is learned and practised: prayer, action and suffering, and judgement.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Bento XVI sobre a esperança cristã, partindo de «Spe salvi facti sumus» (Rm 8,24) para mostrar que a fé é uma esperança performativa, não mera informação. Percorre a Escritura e a Igreja primitiva, critica a redução moderna da esperança ao progresso material, e indica três «lugares» onde ela se aprende e exerce: a oração, o agir e sofrer, e o Juízo. Termina invocando Maria, estrela da esperança.

en.text: On St Jerome as the model and teacher of scriptural study, for the fifteenth centenary of his death: his life, his defence of the full divine inspiration and inerrancy of Scripture against those who would limit it, his rules for the literal and the spiritual senses, and his insistence that clergy, religious and laity alike read Scripture daily and find in it the person of Christ.

it.text: Per il sesto centenario della canonizzazione di san Tommaso d'Aquino: ne celebra la santità e la duplice sapienza, acquisita e infusa, proclamandolo Dottore Universale e Dottore Eucaristico. Ne addita la filosofia e la teologia come norma degli studi ecclesiastici, esorta i giovani a imitarne l'umiltà e la castità nella Milizia Angelica, e indice le celebrazioni centenarie con le relative indulgenze.

en.text: Pius XII's first encyclical, issued weeks into the Second World War, on the unity of the human family under Christ the King. It names two errors eroding that unity: forgetting mankind's common origin and equal dignity, and divorcing civil authority from God's law so that the State becomes its own supreme end. Written in what it calls an Hour of Darkness, it appeals for a return to unity through the Church.

Leo XIII's first encyclical on the Rosary, commending it as a defense of the Church against the errors and dangers of the age. Recalling the precedent of St. Dominic and the victory over the Turks attributed to Mary's intercession in the sixteenth century, he asks that the Rosary and the Litany of Loreto be recited publicly throughout October in every parish church, and grants indulgences to those who take part.

Written to the bishops of Poland against the Mariavites, a society of self-styled Mystic Priests formed without episcopal permission around a woman its members held to be divinely inspired. Pius X confirms the 1904 decree suppressing it, refuses their professed submission as belied by their continued defiance of their bishops, and orders that those who persist in rebellion be dealt with severely.

Why the world has no true peace after the Great War: treaties that never reached the hearts of men, and a chronic war between the social classes. Against this Pius XI sets the peace of Christ, an effect of love rather than of justice alone; he calls the laity to disciplined cooperation with their bishops, condemns a moral, legal and social modernism, and closes protesting the unresolved Roman Question.

Pius X's follow-up encyclical to the French clergy and people on the aftermath of the 1905 Law of Separation, defending the Church's refusal to form the associations cultuelles the law required. It refutes the charges that she incited persecution and abandoned her own property, and condemns a newly voted law on public worship as a further act of spoliation aggravating the Separation itself.

John Paul II's 1995 encyclical on ecumenism, tracing the Catholic Church's own commitment to Christian unity through renewal, prayer, and dialogue with the Eastern and Western churches and ecclesial communities. Its final chapter, "Quanta est nobis via?", includes his invitation to other Christian leaders to help him find a way of exercising the papacy's ministry of unity that serves reconciliation rather than division.

Pius X's protest against the 1905 French Law of Separation, addressed to the cardinals, bishops, clergy and people of France. It rejects separation of Church and state as “a thesis absolutely false” that denies God public worship and confines the state to this life alone, then itemises the law's injuries — the seizure of ecclesiastical property and pious foundations — before calling French Catholics to unity with their bishops and the Holy See.

es.text: Protesta de Pío X contra la Ley francesa de Separación de 1905, dirigida a los cardenales, obispos, clero y pueblo de Francia. Rechaza la separación entre la Iglesia y el Estado como «una tesis absolutamente falsa», que niega a Dios el culto público y confina al Estado a esta sola vida; enumera después los daños de la ley —la incautación de los bienes eclesiásticos y de las fundaciones pías— antes de llamar a los católicos franceses a la unión con sus obispos y con la Santa Sede.

fr.text: Protestation de Pie X contre la loi française de Séparation de 1905, adressée aux cardinaux, évêques, clergé et peuple de France. Elle rejette la séparation de l'Église et de l'État comme « une thèse absolument fausse », qui refuse à Dieu le culte public et enferme l'État dans cette seule vie ; elle énumère ensuite les atteintes de la loi — la saisie des biens ecclésiastiques et des fondations pieuses — avant d'appeler les catholiques français à l'union avec leurs évêques et avec le Saint-Siège.

it.text: Protesta di Pio X contro la legge francese di Separazione del 1905, indirizzata ai cardinali, ai vescovi, al clero e al popolo di Francia. Respinge la separazione tra Chiesa e Stato come «una tesi assolutamente falsa», che nega a Dio il culto pubblico e confina lo Stato a questa sola vita; enumera poi i danni della legge — la confisca dei beni ecclesiastici e delle fondazioni pie — prima di chiamare i cattolici francesi all'unione con i loro vescovi e con la Santa Sede.

pt.text: Protesto de Pio X contra a Lei francesa de Separação de 1905, dirigido aos cardeais, bispos, clero e povo de França. Rejeita a separação entre a Igreja e o Estado como «uma tese absolutamente falsa», que nega a Deus o culto público e confina o Estado a esta vida apenas; enumera depois os danos da lei — a apropriação dos bens eclesiásticos e das fundações pias — antes de chamar os católicos franceses à união com os seus bispos e com a Santa Sé.

en.text: John Paul II's encyclical to the bishops on the foundations of Catholic moral theology, written amid dissent from the Church's moral teaching. Framed by Christ's dialogue with the rich young man — “Teacher, what good must I do to have eternal life?” — it treats freedom's dependence on truth and God's law, conscience, the moral act, and intrinsically evil acts, closing with an appeal to Mary, Mother of Mercy.

pt.text: Carta encíclica de Pio XI aos bispos dos Estados Unidos, elogiando a «Legião da Decência» e tratando da moral cristã diante do cinema. Descreve o poder das imagens, aliadas ao som e à música, sobre grandes públicos em salas escuras, e propõe meios de vigilância: compromisso anual dos fiéis, boletins de classificação e juntas nacionais de bispos e leigos para fiscalizar a produção e a exibição de filmes.

en.text: Vatican II's decree on the Church's missionary activity, grounded in the Trinitarian missions of the Son and the Spirit. It treats mission work itself — witness, preaching, and the gathering of a Christian community — then the young particular churches it plants, the calling and training of missionaries, the planning of missionary work, and the cooperation owed by bishops, priests, religious, and laity.

pt.text: Decreto conciliar sobre a actividade missionária da Igreja: funda a missão no desígnio do Pai e no envio do Filho e do Espírito Santo, e trata do testemunho cristão, da pregação do Evangelho e da formação das comunidades cristãs, das Igrejas particulares, da vocação e formação dos missionários, da organização da obra missionária e do dever de cooperação de bispos, sacerdotes, institutos e leigos.

en.text: Vatican II's decree on the apostolate of the laity, holding that the call to spread Christ's kingdom and renew the temporal order belongs to every layperson through Baptism and Confirmation, not by clerical delegation. It surveys the apostolate's aims, its fields — church, family, youth, social and international life — its individual and organized forms, right relations with the hierarchy, and formation.

pt.text: Decreto do Concílio Vaticano II sobre o apostolado dos leigos: a vocação apostólica que brota da vocação cristã comum, os fins do apostolado — evangelização e santificação do mundo, instauração cristã da ordem temporal, acção caritativa —, os campos em que se exerce (família, juventude, meio social, ordem nacional e internacional), as formas individuais e associadas, a relação com a Hierarquia e a formação exigida aos leigos.

en.text: Vatican II's decree on the pastoral office of bishops. It treats first their place in the college united with the pope — instituting the Synod of Bishops and calling for a reorganized Roman Curia — then the diocesan bishop's governance of his own particular church, in its boundaries, auxiliaries, curia, clergy and religious, and finally cooperation among bishops through episcopal conferences, ecclesiastical provinces, and inter-diocesan offices such as military vicariates.

pt.text: Decreto do Concílio Vaticano II sobre o múnus pastoral dos Bispos na Igreja. Trata do papel dos Bispos na Igreja universal, com o Sínodo episcopal e a renovação da Cúria Romana; do Bispo na sua diocese, porção do Povo de Deus confiada a um pastor, e dos seus deveres de ensinar, santificar e reger; dos seus cooperadores; e das Conferências episcopais e da revisão das circunscrições.

en.text: The Second Vatican Council's dogmatic constitution on divine revelation. It describes revelation as God speaking to human beings as friends through deeds and words together, with Christ as both mediator and fullness; sets Scripture and Tradition as one deposit under the Church's teaching office; and holds that the inspired books teach without error the truth God wanted written for salvation. It closes by urging that all preaching, and the reading of all the faithful, be fed from Scripture.

pt.text: Constituição dogmática do Concílio Vaticano II sobre a Revelação divina: como Deus se revela e se comunica ao homem em Cristo, a sua transmissão pela sagrada Tradição e pela Sagrada Escritura sob a vigilância do Magistério, a inspiração e a verdade dos livros do Antigo e do Novo Testamento, e o lugar da Escritura na vida, no estudo e na leitura da Igreja.

en.text: Vatican II's declaration that the human person has a right to religious freedom: immunity from coercion, by individuals or government, in professing any religion, alone or in community. It argues the right rests first on human dignity and reason, then on revelation — since Christ invited faith rather than compelling it — and urges governments to secure it as a civil right within the bounds of just public order.

pt.text: Declaração do Concílio Vaticano II sobre a liberdade religiosa: afirma que a pessoa humana tem direito à liberdade religiosa, entendida como imunidade de coacção em matéria religiosa, em privado e em público, só ou associada a outros. Expõe primeiro a doutrina geral, fundada na dignidade da pessoa humana e na razão, e depois mostra-a radicada na Revelação divina e no comportamento de Cristo e dos Apóstolos.

en.text: The Church in the modern world, opening in solidarity with “the joys and the hopes, the griefs and the anxieties” of the age and addressed not only to the Church's own members but to the whole of humanity. Part I treats the dignity of the human person, human community, and human activity in the world; Part II takes up marriage and family, culture, economic and social life, the political community, and the fostering of peace among nations.

pt.text: Constituição pastoral do Vaticano II sobre a Igreja no mundo actual, que começa por fazer suas «as alegrias e as esperanças, as tristezas e as angústias» de toda a humanidade. A primeira parte trata a dignidade da pessoa humana, a comunidade humana e a actividade humana no mundo; a segunda, o matrimónio e a família, a cultura, a vida económico-social e política, e a promoção da paz entre as nações.

en.text: Vatican II's declaration on Christian education, opening from every person's inalienable right to an education suited to their nature and final end. It sets out parents as the first educators, the Church's own role in forming the baptized, and the purpose of Catholic schools, colleges, universities and faculties of sacred sciences, closing with a call for coordination among Catholic educational institutions.

pt.text: Declaração conciliar sobre a educação cristã, que parte do direito inalienável de todo o homem a uma educação correspondente à sua dignidade de pessoa. Afirma os pais como primeiros educadores, o papel próprio da Igreja na formação cristã dos baptizados, e a missão das escolas católicas, das universidades católicas e das faculdades de ciências sagradas, terminando com um apelo à coordenação entre as instituições escolares católicas.

en.text: The Council's decree on the media of social communications — press, cinema, radio, television. It claims the Church's right to use them and her duty to teach their right use, sets out the moral principles binding on those who make and those who consume them, including the claims of art and the protection of the young, and charges pastors, laity and a Roman office with a common apostolate.

pt.text: Decreto do Vaticano II sobre a imprensa, o cinema, o rádio e a televisão. Reconhece nestes meios um dom que a Igreja usa para a evangelização, mas que pode voltar-se contra o homem, e fixa normas morais para o seu recto uso — a formação da consciência, a relação entre arte e moral, os deveres de autores e destinatários. Propõe ainda a imprensa católica e um dia mundial em seu favor.

en.text: The Council's dogmatic constitution on the Church: the mystery of the Church as sacrament and as People of God, then her hierarchical structure and the episcopate, the vocation of the laity, the universal call to holiness, the religious life, the pilgrim Church's bond with the Church in heaven, and last the place of Mary in the mystery of Christ and the Church.

pt.text: Constituição dogmática do Concílio Vaticano II sobre a Igreja, chamada luz dos povos e sacramento da união com Deus. Percorre o mistério da Igreja como povo de Deus e corpo de Cristo, sua constituição hierárquica de bispos, presbíteros e diáconos, a vocação dos leigos, o chamamento universal à santidade, a vida religiosa e a índole escatológica da Igreja peregrina, terminando com o lugar de Maria no mistério de Cristo e da Igreja.

en.text: Vatican II's declaration on the Church's relationship to non-Christian religions, moving from the questions common to all peoples about the meaning of existence through Hinduism and Buddhism, Islam, and above all Judaism, whose spiritual patrimony with Christianity it traces to Abraham and whose collective guilt for Christ's death it repudiates. It closes by rejecting all discrimination on grounds of race, color, condition, or religion.

pt.text: Sobre a relação da Igreja com as religiões não-cristãs: parte das origens comuns da humanidade e das grandes perguntas existenciais, passa pelo hinduísmo, o budismo e o islão, detém-se longamente no vínculo espiritual entre cristãos e judeus — repudiando a culpa coletiva pela morte de Cristo e todo antissemitismo — e termina exortando à fraternidade universal contra a discriminação racial ou religiosa.

en.text: Vatican II's decree on the training of future priests, requiring each episcopal conference to draft a national program adapting formation to local conditions. It treats the fostering of vocations, the organization of major seminaries, and a spiritual formation modeled on Christ the priest, then calls for ecclesiastical studies reorganized around the mystery of Christ with Scripture as theology's soul, adding pastoral training and formation continuing after ordination.

pt.text: Decreto do Concílio Vaticano II sobre a formação sacerdotal. Situa o dever de promover as vocações em toda a comunidade cristã, propõe um plano nacional de formação adaptável pelas Conferências episcopais e organiza os seminários maiores em torno de quatro eixos: formação espiritual cristocêntrica, revisão dos estudos eclesiásticos (filosofia e teologia), formação estritamente pastoral e formação complementar após o curso do seminário.

en.text: The Council's decree on the Eastern Catholic Churches — those in communion with Rome that follow the Byzantine, Alexandrian, Antiochene, Armenian or Chaldean rites rather than the Latin. It affirms their equal dignity with the Latin Church and their right to keep their own liturgical, disciplinary and spiritual patrimony, then treats patriarchal precedence, the discipline of the sacraments, worship and the calendar, and what common prayer with separated Eastern Christians is permitted.

pt.text: Decreto do Concílio Vaticano II sobre as Igrejas Orientais Católicas: afirma a igual dignidade dos seus ritos e patriarcas, defende a conservação e restauração do património litúrgico e disciplinar oriental — sacramentos, calendário pascal, línguas vernáculas —, e estabelece normas sobre matrimónios mistos e sobre a communicatio in sacris com os irmãos orientais separados, em vista da unidade plena.

en.text: Vatican II's decree on the renewal and adaptation of religious life, addressed to institutes of consecrated chastity, poverty and obedience. It lays down general principles of renewal — return to the Gospel and to each institute's founding spirit, adaptation to modern conditions — treats the contemplative, active, monastic, lay and secular-institute forms in turn, and gives norms on formation, cloister, habit, vocations, and the union of small communities.

pt.text: Decreto do Concílio Vaticano II sobre a renovação da vida religiosa, ligada ao regresso às fontes evangélicas e ao espírito dos fundadores. Percorre os institutos contemplativos, apostólicos e monásticos, a vida religiosa laical e os institutos seculares, os votos de castidade, pobreza e obediência, a vida comum, a clausura, o hábito e a formação, e conclui exortando os religiosos a corresponder com generosidade à sua vocação.

en.text: Vatican II's decree on the ministry and life of priests. It grounds the priesthood in Christ's own priestly office, then treats priests' ministry of preaching, sacraments and pastoral leadership, their relationships with bishops, fellow priests and the laity, and the vocation to holiness through obedience, celibacy and poverty, closing with an exhortation amid the difficulties of contemporary priestly life.

pt.text: Decreto do Concílio Vaticano II sobre o ministério e a vida dos sacerdotes. Trata da natureza do presbiterado na missão da Igreja, das funções dos presbíteros — pregação da palavra, sacramentos e cura pastoral — e das suas relações com os bispos, entre si e com os leigos; depois, da vida espiritual dos presbíteros, chamados à perfeição, com o celibato, a pobreza voluntária e a formação permanente.

en.text: The Council's constitution ordering a general restoration of the liturgy, directed at the full, conscious and active participation of the faithful. It lays down the principles of that reform and then works chapter by chapter through the Eucharist, the other sacraments and the sacramentals, the Divine Office, the liturgical year, sacred music and sacred art, admitting a wider use of the vernacular throughout.

pt.text: Estabelece os princípios gerais da reforma e do incremento da Liturgia, pedindo a participação plena, consciente e activa dos fiéis nas celebrações. Organiza-se em capítulos sobre a Eucaristia, os demais sacramentos e sacramentais, o Ofício Divino, o ano litúrgico, a música sacra, e a arte sacra e as alfaias litúrgicas, com um apêndice sobre a revisão do calendário.

en.text: The Council's decree on the restoration of unity among Christians, whose divisions it holds to be against Christ's will. It sets out the Catholic principles of ecumenism, including the elements of sanctification found in separated communities, treats its practice as rooted in interior conversion and dialogue, and considers separately the Eastern Churches and the communities separated from Rome in the West.

pt.text: Decreto do Concílio Vaticano II sobre o ecumenismo. Parte da unidade que Cristo quis para a Igreja e das rupturas surgidas desde os primeiros séculos — no Oriente por controvérsias dogmáticas, no Ocidente pela Reforma — para expor os princípios católicos do movimento ecuménico: renovação interior, conversão do coração, oração e diálogo com os irmãos separados. Examina depois, em separado, as Igrejas orientais e as comunidades ocidentais separadas de Roma.
